items.text:
MANSFIELD, Texas -- The United States was not leaving any room for doubt.
It entered Friday's Concacaf W Championship quarterfinal as the heavy favorites against El Salvador, and the U.S. rolled 8-0 at Texas Health Mansfield Stadium to qualify for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil.
The eight goals by the U.S. are the most in a game under coach Emma Hayes and the most for the women's team in a game since 2022, when it beat Uzbekistan 9-0 in a friendly. The U.S. will play Jamaica, which beat Costa Rica earlier in the day, in the semifinals on Tuesday.
"I said congratulations to the team, but this is a tournament and we want to win the tournament, so I'm only thinking about our next game against Jamaica," Hayes said after the game. "Of course, since the Olympics, our next goal was to qualify for the World Cup. We've now done that, but we haven't achieved anything, we've just qualified for the World Cup."
Forward Ashley Sanchez scored a hat trick in less than seven minutes, one of the fastest in team history, to lead the USWNT's seven-goal first half during Friday's quarterfinal that served as a direct qualifier for the 2027 World Cup.
The USWNT has qualified for all 10 World Cups to date and has won four of them.
U.S. defender Kennedy Wesley opened the scoring nine minutes into the match Friday, when she redirected a cross from Sophia Wilson into the net. El Salvador goalkeeper Riley Meléndez deflected the cross, but Wesley was one of five unmarked U.S. players in the box.
Wesley's U.S. center back partner, Tierna Davidson, doubled the lead in the 31st minute, when she headed in a precise free kick from Mallory Swanson, who added a goal a minute later.
"I don't think it's any less special. I think every time that we're able to qualify this team for a World Cup is something that we're really excited about," Davidson said. "We've been preparing for it for years, but to be able to mark it in Sharpie on calendars now is something that we're really happy about."
Sanchez then went on her hat trick run, which included a sublime upper-corner finish for her second goal, and Wilson added the United States' seventh goal just before halftime.
It was Sanchez's first multigoal game for the U.S. after scoring against Spain last month, when she returned to the squad for the first time in nearly two years. She was named NWSL MVP last week after scoring a record-tying 20 goals this season.
"I think it was a really big accomplishment what I did at club, and I was just trying to feed off that, feed off the consistency that I had there, and bring it here and just try my best," Sanchez told Paramount Plus after her big night.
Friday marked just the third time in history that the U.S. women scored seven goals in the first half of a game, and the first since 2012 Olympic qualifying against the Dominican Republic, per ESPN Global Research. All three instances have come against Concacaf opponents.
Croix Bethune came off the bench to add the eighth goal in the second half.
All four quarterfinal winners at the Concacaf W Championship will qualify for the 2027 World Cup. Earlier on Friday, Jamaica booked its World Cup spot for the third straight time.
The U.S. and Canada advanced to the quarterfinals automatically as the top two teams in the region. El Salvador was playing in its first Concacaf W Championship match Friday after winning its group in the previous phase of qualifying.
The United States played world No. 1 Spain in the October window, falling 2-0 in the opening match before a 2-2 draw in the second.
"I love nothing more than something you work on, you bring it to life in a game. And that most importantly, they have the belief, the confidence, the conviction to do it again and again," Hayes added. "I've said this to the team, I've said it publicly: We create as many chances as Japan and Spain in world football. We don't score as many goals as those two teams, and that is a gap for us to close.
"I think you saw tonight the decisiveness that I've been speaking about in multiple press conferences, and this is the expectation that we demand. And the players lived up to that, and I'm super proud of it."
Some unfamiliarity with the stage was evident from before the opening whistle. Team captains usually exchange pennants during handshakes, but El Salvador's Brenda Ceren forgot her team's pennant in the locker room, prompting a brief delay pregame. An El Salvador staff member ran out of the locker room in the north end zone of the 7,000-seat stadium to hand the pennant to be exchanged with U.S. captain Lindsey Heaps.
El Salvador struggled to string together multiple passes throughout the match. After the fourth U.S. goal, El Salvador defender Victoria Meza and head coach Eric Acuña had a heated exchange on the sidelines.
Acuña was rebuked by the team's players and the El Salvadorian federation last month for comments about the team after back-to-back losses to Paraguay. He said he was removing all privileges from players, such as coffee outings, and he questioned the quality of his players. He kept his job despite the backlash.
Earlier this week, the El Salvadorian federation announced that it would pay players a $1 million total bonus if they qualify for the World Cup for the first time.
El Salvador still has a path to the World Cup. It will play Costa Rica on Saturday in the Concacaf play-in game. The winner will advance to FIFA's global playoff next year, with a World Cup berth on the line.
"It's a wake-up call, it really brings you back down to earth," Acuña said after the game. "When things happen so fast, you can end up in situations where you're no longer in control of what's unfolding, and I think that's exactly what happened. Losing a match 1-0 is the same as losing 9-0.
"I said it from the very beginning, I'm here for the wild-card and the playoff spot. I said that months, maybe even a year ago. I've been very clear about that. The thing is that while I'm the only one who can't afford to dream, the fans have e

items.title: Columbus dumps Miami, Messi from MLS playoffs with extra-time winner
items.summary:
Defending champions Inter Miami and Lionel Messi were eliminated from the 2026 MLS playoffs after a 1-0 loss against the Columbus Crew in the second game of the Round 1, best-of-three series Friday night.
The No. 7 seed Crew won the first game of the series 3-0 on Nov. 21 at Nu Stadium and entered F
items.text:
Defending champions Inter Miami and Lionel Messi were eliminated from the 2026 MLS playoffs after a 1-0 loss against the Columbus Crew in the second game of the Round 1, best-of-three series Friday night.
The No. 7 seed Crew won the first game of the series 3-0 on Nov. 21 at Nu Stadium and entered Friday's game at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in Ohio with the advantage.
Santiago Rodríguez scored a stunning late goal for Columbus, volleying home from close range after a goalmouth scramble minutes before the full-time whistle and just before the game would have gone to a penalty shootout to decide the winner.
The Crew held Messi in check in both games, frustrating the World Cup winner and limiting his space and chances. They also kept Miami's big preseason signing Germán Berterame at bay. The Mexico international missed two chances in Game 2, including a header right in front of goal that would have given Miami a lead late.
"We created the clearest scoring opportunities. But that's football for you," Miami manager Kily Gonzalez said after the match. "Naturally, we are feeling a profound sense of sadness and disappointment. Our season has come to an end.
"Even though Leó didn't threaten [the Crew] goal much, they held their own. It's not just about outplaying the opponent, it's about scoring goals, and today we simply couldn't convert. Right before their goal, we had a chance with Germán Berterame, he was right in front of the net which would have secured the win.
"We were up against an opponent that clearly understands how Inter plays and took the necessary precautions to defend their defensive third. We generated plenty of chances, but we couldn't quite find a way to counter their deep-lying, five-man defensive line."
The Crew earned their eighth straight win and their 10th victory in 12 games to send Laurent Courtois' side into the Eastern Conference semifinals after having been in last place at the beginning of September.
"The process that we had the last few months, it paid off, and the guys stuck to the plan," Courtois said after the game. "They had each other's backs, when it was tough, they stuck to what we believed was going to be successful for us, and tonight, they played against a great team, they showed what they can do."
Part of that process was bringing Rodriguez back to MLS, with the former New York City FC striker joining the Crew at the start of September, right at the start of the team's turnaround.
"It was surprising to see the position the team was in when I arrived because in the first trainings I saw the quality of the team," Rodriguez said. "Honestly I didn't understand it. But what we accomplished now is what we were prepared for.
"There is a lot of quality here, maybe a little bit of passion or fight was lacking but maybe with my arrival and Brais Méndez, because we fight a little more. It motivates the whole team and that is very important we see it in all the games because the fans also feel well represented.'
It's the second time since Messi joined Inter Miami in 2023 that the team lost in the first round of the playoffs after falling to Atlanta United FC in the third game of the best-of-three series in 2024.
The loss to Columbus marks the first time the Herons were eliminated in the first round in just two matches and the first time they were shutout in consecutive games since 2023.
"The first match, obviously, set the tone, it defined the parameters of the series," Gonzalez said. "We knew what had happened in that first game, and we had to try to turn the situation around. In my view, the team rose to the occasion; at times, we even outplayed them. We didn't concede as many chances as we had been, certainly not as many as in the previous match. Defensively, the team performed well, but we lacked that bit of finesse in the final third to finish off our plays."
Messi finished the 2026 season with 26 goals and 17 assists and once again won the MLS Golden Boot, but the team had shown cracks all season, with a lackluster record at home and just one win against another playoff team since the middle of July.
Miami heads into the offseason with several tournaments to prepare for in 2027, including the MLS sprint season, the Concacaf Champions Cup and the Leagues Cup.
The team is expected to announce end-of-the-year-roster decisions in the coming days.
Inter Miami will kick off the 2027 MLS campaign Feb. 19, with a home game against FC Cincinnati at Nu Stadium.

items.title: Fofana booed by Chelsea fans, then booked, subbed off amid ire over interview
items.summary:
Chelsea fans booed Wesley Fofana during the early stages of the visit to Nottingham Forest after the Blues defender's controversial unauthorized interview and endured a harrowing night on the pitch at the City Ground.
The center back gave away a penalty for a rash foul that was converted by Morgan G
items.text:
Chelsea fans booed Wesley Fofana during the early stages of the visit to Nottingham Forest after the Blues defender's controversial unauthorized interview and endured a harrowing night on the pitch at the City Ground.
The center back gave away a penalty for a rash foul that was converted by Morgan Gibbs-White and was susbequently substituted by Xabi Alonso before the hour mark in the game.
The Blues' defensive woes saw them fall to a 3-2 defeat to Forest, their third successive defeat in the Premier League.
Fofana has emerged as the scapegoat for Chelsea's dip in form. He drew criticism earlier in the week for talking for almost two hours with French YouTuber Zack Nani on a range of topics, admitting that he came close to quitting football while he was sidelined with an ACL injury, while also appearing to joke about missing his penalty during last month's Carabao Cup shootout defeat to Liverpool.
Fofana apologized for the interview and Alonso said the matter was closed, but visiting supporters were less forgiving.
They jeered their own player when he was in possession.
It has been a particularly difficult spell for Fofana, who has been singled out for poor performances during the team's bad run. His poor form carried into the City Ground, where his error and subsequent foul on Liam Delap saw him concede a penalty early in the second half.
- Raheem Sterling avoids jail for dangerous driving
- Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners
Chelsea had endured a tough start at the City Ground as they fell behind to Igor Jesus' brilliant fifth-minute strike. Gibbs-White's penalty doubled the hosts' lead soon after the break.
Fofana's foul on Delap earned him a booking and led to Alonso taking him off in the 56th minute in favor of Levi Colwill. He went off with Chelsea fans chanting "f--- off, Fofana, you're not wanted here."
Substitute Emmanuel Emegha scored a brace after coming on at halftime but Gibbs-White's second of the game, which came between Emegha's goals, ultimately proved the difference for Forest.
The result keeps Chelsea in eighth place, 12 points behind leaders Arsenal, and raises the pressure on Alonso. The scrutiny is centered on their defensive showings, with the Blues having conceded 23 goals this season in 12 matches. It is the joint-worst record in the Premier League.
"Well, we have to stick together, and everyone that is in the changing room, everyone in the team is needed," Alonso said.
"We need to help, and we need to go through these tough moments all together, and we don't leave anyone apart.
"We need to support everyone. That is because we need everyone, and we need the fans.
"We need all the players. We need to stick together because if not, things will get more complicated, and that's what we want to do."
Asked whether the Chelsea fans' reaction to Fofana made it more difficult to pick him going forward, he added: "Well, I'm thinking right after the game and for the next games, we will see."
Information from PA contributed to this report.

Two staff members of Doctors Without Borders, the humanitarian relief agency known by its French initials MSF, have b
items.text:
Israeli strike on Doctors Without Borders clinic in Gaza kills two staff
MSF says Israeli attack on Gaza clinic a ‘direct hit’ and calls for those responsible to be held accountable.
Two staff members of Doctors Without Borders, the humanitarian relief agency known by its French initials MSF, have been killed in an Israeli strike on one of its clinics in Gaza City.
“We are devastated and outraged by the killing of two of our colleagues, both watchmen, in an Israeli strike on one of our Gaza clinics tonight,” MSF said on X on Friday.
It called the attack a “direct hit” and said the deaths bring the number of its staff killed in Gaza to 17.
The agency’s premises were “clearly marked with MSF logos, and their location had been communicated to and was known by the Israeli military”, the group said.
It called for those responsible to be held accountable.
In a statement following the strike, the Israeli military claimed, without providing evidence, that the two workers were members of Hamas.
World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called the attack “outrageous and unacceptable”.
“Those risking their lives to save others must be protected, not attacked,” he wrote on X.
The Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor condemned the “attack on a clearly marked MSF clinic” and accused Israel of “systematic targeting of humanitarian personnel and facilities”.
A pattern of attacks
Israeli forces have killed more than 1,700 health workers in Gaza, including 15 MSF staff as of January.
In January, MSF said Israel had blocked its supplies and denied entry to all its international staff since the start of the year.
Israeli officials have alleged, without proof, that aid groups are linked to Hamas, while aid organisations say such accusations have helped normalise attacks on humanitarian workers.
Earlier this week, an Israeli strike in Gaza killed Adel al-Helou, who had worked for 35 years for UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestinian refugees.
Al-Helou was supplying water to residents of the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza. Three other people were wounded in the attack, UNRWA and medics said.
The strike came despite a ceasefire that took effect in October 2025, which Israel has repeatedly violated.

items.text:
Parts of US clean up after Thanksgiving storm lashes East Coast
Power is being slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers following a round of heavy wind, rain and snow.
Heavy rain and flooding have begun to ease along the US East Coast as power is being slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers following a round of holiday storms.
The storms disrupted travel and downed trees and power lines, leading to water rescues in multiple states, from New York to Virginia.
In New York City, preparations were under way for the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on Saturday after an unprecedented postponement because of rain and high winds.
The parade, an annual spectacle usually held on Thanksgiving Day, sees brightly coloured balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan. The festivities also kick off the holiday shopping season for the US.
The same balloons and floats, and most of the original celebrities, are still set to take part, organisers said.
Elsewhere, wet snow fell as far south as the Tennessee Valley and freezing rain moved across northern New England. Cold rain was reported in parts of the Midwest, including the Ohio Valley and the lower Great Lakes.
While conditions are expected to improve across the entire eastern US, the National Weather Service warned that “this huge system will take some time to weaken”.
The low-pressure system that brought the storm to the East Coast, the service added, would continue to slowly exit to the northeast, “bringing lingering showers and isolated freezing precipitation through Saturday”.
Coastal flood warnings were also issued in several states from New Jersey to Virginia.
Power restored, travel disruptions ease
The number of power outages, which peaked on Thursday at more than 900,000, fell to 264,000 by Friday evening as crews worked to restore electricity, according to poweroutage.us.
Pennsylvania had the most, followed by Missouri.
Some flight disruptions also lingered on Friday, with about 1,600 delays and more than 500 cancellations, according to the tracking service FlightAware.
In the southern US, part of Tennessee was under a winter storm warning for up to 2.5cm (one inch) of snow on Friday, after rain turned into light snow on Thanksgiving.
In the Midwest, conditions were calmer than they were the previous day, when as much as 38cm (15 inches) of snow fell in eastern Missouri.
The weather service said heavy snow was still expected in parts of Montana and Wyoming, however.
Along the Pacific coast, waves driven by high tides caused flooding and continued to affect train services. Record tides along the California coast prompted evacuations from Humboldt County in the far north to Ventura County near Los Angeles.

items.text:
Polls open in Taiwan's closely watched local elections
November 28, 2026
Taiwan's voters begun choosing mayors and county chiefs in local elections on Saturday that may gauge the mood ahead of the island's 2028 presidential elections.
Polls close at 4 p.m. (0800 UTC/GMT) and results are expected by early evening. Winners will serve four-year terms.
Most candidates are from the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) or the Nationalist Party, also known as the Kuomintang or KMT. The latter has traditionally performed better in local elections and favors closer ties with China.
President Lai Ching-te has campaigned for candidates from his DPP.
Closely watched in Beijing
China is paying close attention, despite not currently featuring as a key campaign issue. Taiwan's government warned its people to be vigilant against fake news on social media, citing a Chinese disinformation campaign.
Taiwan's 22 cities and counties are currently focused on issues such as transport, childcare and the environment. While these issues do not directly impact the China policy, Beijing has repeatedly weighed in.
China denounced the governing Democratic Progressive candidate for Taipei's mayoral race, Puma Shen, who is wanted by Chinese police for alleged "separatist activities." He entered the mayoral race as an underdog but has managed to ride a political wave that drew huge crowds to his campaign rallies.
Earlier this month, Shen said Chinese police had never contacted him and that whoever wins, Taipei's election would be a victory for democracy in the face of pressure from Beijing.
If Shen wins, he would be the capital city's first DPP mayor in nearly 30 years. This result could be seen as "quite shameful" in Beijing, according to Austin Wang, political science professor at the University of Nevada.
China claims Taiwan as part of its territory under its "One China" principle and has recently increased pressure on Taiwan to accept its sovereignty claims, threatening force to seize the island.
Taipei's incumbent and KMT member, Mayor Chiang Wan-an has campaigned against Shen, also pulling in thousands of supporters to his rallies. In the last election, KMT thrashed DPP, winning 14 of the 22 cities and counties while the DPP won only five. Chiang is also seen as a potential future presidential candidate.
What impact could the vote have on presidential elections?
Analysts have cautioned that the local elections are not a reliable barometer of how people might vote for the presidential elections in 2028. Still, Saturday's results could influence the selection process for the KMT presidential candidate.
The DPP is likely to rally behind President Lai for a reelection.
The most likely KMT candidates are Taichung's outgoing Mayor Lu Shiow-yen and parliamentary speaker Han Kuo-yu.
KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun, who's pro-Beijing stance has even alienated her from many in the party, is also viewed as a potential challenger for the party's nomination. However, she could face pressure to step down if KMT performs poorly in the local elections.

Taiwan votes in local elections to choose mayors, other leaders
Key mayoral race in Taipei, a stronghold of the opposition Kuomintang, tests the governing Democratic Progressive Party.
Taiwan is choosing mayors, council members and other local leaders across its 22 cities and counties in an election
items.text:
Taiwan votes in local elections to choose mayors, other leaders
Key mayoral race in Taipei, a stronghold of the opposition Kuomintang, tests the governing Democratic Progressive Party.
Taiwan is choosing mayors, council members and other local leaders across its 22 cities and counties in an election that has been unusually competitive in some of the island’s biggest cities.
Polls opened at 8am (00:00 GMT) on Saturday and will close at 4pm (08:00 GMT), with results expected early in the evening.
Voters are casting ballots at schools, temples and community centres.
About 11,000 positions are at stake in the “nine-in-one” elections, named for the nine categories of local government posts being contested.
The Taipei race
A key contest is for the mayor of the capital, Taipei, a traditional stronghold of the opposition Kuomintang (KMT).
Mayor Chiang Wan-an of the KMT, who won by a double-digit margin in the last election and is seen as a possible future presidential candidate, faces a strong challenge from Puma Shen of the governing Democratic Progressive Party (DPP).
Shen is an academic-turned-lawmaker and an expert on China’s information warfare. China has denounced him, and Chinese police say he is wanted for “separatism”. He entered the race as the underdog, but has drawn huge crowds at his rallies.
Shen’s victory in the KMT’s heartland could be seen as “quite shameful” in Beijing, said Austin Wang, a political scientist at the University of Nevada.
Chiang told supporters the race was “very close”.
Shen cancelled a final rally over traffic concerns and held an online event instead, which drew more than 500,000 viewers on YouTube. President William Lai Ching-te of the DPP also urged voters at a rally in neighbouring New Taipei City to back the party’s candidates there.
Other notable races are in New Taipei City, Taiwan’s most populous city, and Kaohsiung, in the south. New Taipei City’s incumbent mayor is from the KMT, while Kaohsiung’s mayoral office is held by the DPP.
China’s pressure
The vote will not directly change Taiwan’s China policy, and campaigns have focused on local issues such as transport, childcare and the environment.
Beijing, which claims Taiwan as its own territory, has repeatedly weighed in, and the vote is being closely watched there.
Taiwan’s Defence Ministry said it tracked 30 Chinese military aircraft around the island on Friday, 26 of which crossed the median line of the Taiwan Strait in a “joint combat readiness patrol” with warships.
Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council has warned that Beijing is trying to influence the outcome through “cognitive warfare” and “transnational repression”.
China’s Defence Ministry said this week that “reunification” is an unstoppable trend.
In the last local elections four years ago, the KMT won 14 cities and counties, the DPP five and other parties or independents three. The KMT traditionally favours closer ties with Beijing, while the DPP rejects China’s sovereignty claims.
Analysts say local results are an unreliable guide to the outcome of the next presidential election, due in early 2028. Lai is expected to seek a second term.
The KMT could begin debating its presidential ticket soon after the vote. The likely candidates include outgoing Taichung Mayor Lu Shiow-yen and parliamentary speaker Han Kuo-yu.
KMT chairwoman Cheng Li-wun, who met Chinese President Xi Jinping in April, is also seen as a possible challenger, though she could face pressure to step down if the party does badly.

items.text:
Nigeria's 'ultimate hard man' who become an online meme
- Published
For generations of Nigerians, Pete Edochie was more than a celebrated actor.
He was Okonkwo – the fierce, proud and troubled warrior whose portrayal in Things Fall Apart made him a household name and earned him a place in the hearts of millions.
Even in death, many Nigerians still refer to him by the character's name, a testament to the enduring impact of a role that defined his career.
Edochie died on 25 November, aged 79, in the south-eastern Nigerian city of Enugu following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.
In 1987, Edochie starred in a television adaptation of Chinua Achebe's acclaimed novel. His portrayal of Okonkwo would change his life, establishing him as one of Nigeria's most respected actors and bringing him international recognition.
The series depicted the struggles of an African community as British colonial rule and Christianity began to transform its traditional way of life.
Joy Nnamdi, a fan of both the novel and its television adaptation, believes Edochie was the perfect choice for the lead role.
She said nobody else could have brought the character to life as convincingly.
"His character Okonkwo gave a face to the highly celebrated novel," she told the BBC in Nigeria's biggest city, Lagos.
The role also cemented his reputation as a hard man, a screen persona he would maintain through much of his career.
"It was very rare to see him laugh in movies. He was the ultimate tough man," Nnamdi added.
With his deep, authoritative voice, imposing presence and effortless command of African proverbs, Edochie had a way of dominating a scene without raising his voice.
Whether playing a village elder, a wealthy businessman or a feared traditional ruler, he became an enduring embodiment of patriarchal authority on screen.
Edochie went on to become one of the most recognisable faces of Nollywood, Nigeria's film industry, which has grown into one of the world's largest.
From Kenya to South Africa, MultiChoice's Africa Magic channels helped take his films into millions of African homes as Nollywood became a cultural phenomenon across the continent.
Although many of his films were rooted in his Igbo culture, their themes of family loyalty, inheritance disputes, spiritual beliefs and the abuse of power resonated with audiences far beyond Nigeria.
Before becoming a household name in the film industry, however, Edochie had built a successful career in broadcasting.
Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, northern Nigeria, he attended primary and secondary school in Kaduna before studying journalism and television at the School of Journalism and Television in the UK.
He joined the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation in 1967, the year Nigeria's civil war broke out.
He joined the pro-separatist Voice of Biafra, and recently described the war years as the greatest personal challenge he ever faced.
"During the war, the experience that we had as Biafrans, you know, survival was difficult. Hunger was driving us into eating all sorts of nonsense," he recalled.
He rose through the ranks to hold senior management positions but then switched to acting. Over a career spanning several decades, he appeared in numerous films, including Igodo, Rituals and Billionaire's Club.
His career also bridged the transition from home-video productions to global streaming platforms.
The 2018 romantic comedy Lionheart, which became Netflix's first original Nigerian film, introduced his work to a wider international audience.
He also worked in Ghana, where he starred alongside some of the country's biggest film stars in the 2017 comedy John and John.
His contribution to the arts was recognised in 2003 when he received one of Nigeria's national honours, the Member of the Order of the Niger (MON).
He also received several other accolades, including the Industry Merit Award at the Africa Magic Viewers' Choice Awards.
In recent years, Edochie found an unexpected new audience online.
His distinctive facial expressions, witty remarks and memorable scenes from his films became popular social media memes, introducing his work to a younger generation of Africans.
For many who had never watched Things Fall Apart or his early Nollywood films, his stern expressions became a humorous way of conveying disbelief, disapproval or exasperation at everyday situations.
But his reputation as a formidable screen presence was no joke to those who grew up watching him.
Sani Muazu recalls that parents in the northern Nigerian city of Kano would sometimes invoke Edochie's name to keep misbehaving children in check.
"They would tell you: 'Okonkwo will come and visit you if you don't stop' and we would begin acting right," he said.
"To be honest, we grew up scared of him. Even though he was on the screen and not physically present, some of his roles added to our fears because he played some popular occultic roles, and villain roles suited him."
Tributes poured in from fans and fellow actors following news of his death, with many describing him as a giant who helped shape Nigeria's film industry.
Popular actress Genevieve Nnaji paid her tribute in a post on X.
"I will let the assurance of the fact that you are a chosen one; and therefore, have returned to the most high God override my grief and heartbreak. May the heart of a true lion forever rest in peace. We love you," she wrote.
Patience Ozokwor, popularly known as Mama G, who appeared alongside Edochie in several productions, remembered him as a brilliant actor and a source of wisdom.
"He has been a father to stories that are told, like an elder sitting down telling you how things were done in those days," she told BBC News Pidgin.
"I called him any time, any day. He'll tell you what to do and what not to do."
Film director Babangida Bangis told the BBC that Edochie's death was a loss not just for Nigeria or Africa, but for the global film industry.

items.text:
Thousands of Puerto Ricans join ‘Day of National Outrage’ protest
Anger and frustration erupt over record-high electricity rates, surging cost of living and deteriorating basic services.
Thousands of Puerto Ricans have protested in the capital, San Juan, as anger and frustration erupted over record-high electricity rates, the surging cost of living, deteriorating basic services and other issues.
Retirees, university students, bus drivers and others joined Friday’s protest organised by some 30 groups ranging from unions to religious organisations. The crowds gathered in front of a mall for what organisers dubbed the “Day of National Outrage”.
Hundreds of demonstrators arrived by bus in San Juan from dozens of cities and towns across the island.
Asked what problems Puerto Rico had, 74-year-old Radames Garcia Badillo said: “Where to start? The outrage is absolute.”
He said that power and water services are unreliable and that his neighbourhood goes dark at least once a week for several hours. He also decried a sharp increase in the cost of living.
“We’re buying less because things are extremely expensive,” he said. “For us retirees, it is essential to make every dollar stretch.”
The protest, one of the largest in the US territory since Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez took office in January 2025, grew throughout the day as demonstrators took over one of the island’s main highways, forcing its closure.
Organisers estimated that some 8,000 people took part, according to local media.
Many in the crowd waved or wore the Puerto Rican flag. Some chose the flag from before the island became a US commonwealth in 1952, often a sign of cultural pride and sometimes of resistance.
Soaring electricity bills
“Things have never been good in Puerto Rico, but they keep getting worse,” said Veronica Ishtar, a visual arts student.
This week alone, she said the power in her neighbourhood went out 12 times.
In addition, monthly electricity bills for some residential customers recently rose about 18 percent, with the new rate per kilowatt-hour far surpassing the average for residential customers on the US mainland, according to the US Energy Information Administration.
Some protesters blamed Luma Energy, a private company that oversees the transmission and distribution of power on the island.
Puerto Rico’s Supreme Court approved a move to cancel the government’s contract with Luma on Wednesday, but many now worry about what comes next.
Puerto Rico’s Association of Industries said the cancellation could discourage private investment and jeopardise existing projects as crews continue to repair a grid razed by Hurricane Maria in 2017.
The leaders of several groups that organised the protest pledged to keep pushing for change.
“We must begin to channel the rage,” said Hernaliz Vazquez, executive director of Sierra Club Puerto Rico. “We must begin to organise the indignation felt by people who do not know what to do.”

items.text:
Spain's Sanchez makes final appeal to voters before election
November 28, 2026
Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Friday hit the campaign trail one last time before Spaniards head to the polls on Sunday, telling people to "vote, vote, vote" to make sure the country doesn't go "backwards."
Opinion polls point to a change in government, with the conservative People's Party (PP) slated to come out on top, bringing an end to Sanchez's eight years of leftist leadership.
Spain's general election this Sunday is also crucial because it kicks off a round of elections on the continentand because it is yet another test of the region's shift to the right.
The PP would potentially have to rely on support from the far-right anti-immigration Vox party to form the next government in Spain.
There's also a chance that the election ends in a hung parliament, with neither the right-wing coalition nor the left bloc securing a majority.
Sanchez has so far campaigned on a platform of having boosted the Spanish economy when its European Union partners were struggling.
He has pointed to his policies of having increased the minimum wage and having lifted pensions in line with inflation.
But people are frustrated that the cost of living has soared and that they're not able to enjoy the fruits of economic growth, with many unable to leave their parents' house because of very high rental prices.
Sanchez doubles down on attempt to appeal to leftist voters
Sanchez said during his final rally in Madrid that the "elections are about moving Spain forward, not moving it backwards."
He doubled down on an attempt to appeal to left-leaning voters, telling them that a right coalition government, with far-right members in parliament, would reverse the years of social progress and gut public services.
Oscar-winning Spanish film director Pedro Almodovar was also at the rally this evening.
Sanchez wore a red T-shirt that said "the power of the people," telling people that a "progressive majority is within our reach."
Sanchez has also become the standard-bearer for Europeans frustrated with the Trump administration.
PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo dismisses Sanchez's campaign of 'fear'
PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo, who has said that he wants to maintain good relations with US President Donald Trump, dismissed Sanchez's campaign of "fear."
Feijoo won the most seats during elections in 2023, but he was not able to form a government.
"And when a government has nothing to offer but fear, it means it has nothing else left to offer," he told supporters at his campaign finale in the southern city of Seville.
"Governing is about managing, and I have spent my whole life preparing for this moment," said Feijoo, who built his career running central public bodies and the northwestern Galicia region.
He has advocated for tough immigration policies and stronger border management.
Santiago Abascal, the leader of the Vox party, favors a much tougher approach, with his party having advocated for mass deportations.
Addressing a closing rally at a bullring in the eastern city of Valencia, Abascal told supporters not to "vote out of fear. Vote with courage."
"What we are up against is a criminal mafia led by a ruthless boss, a liar," he said, referring to the corruption scandals that have surrounded Sanchez and his government.

items.text:
At least eight found dead on migrant boat off Spain’s Canary Islands
Six people airlifted to hospital in serious condition, Spanish rescue service says.
At least eight migrants have been found dead on a boat carrying about 100 people that was rescued near Spain’s Canary Islands, the Spanish maritime rescue service has said.
The rescue service said on Friday that between eight and 10 bodies were found on board and that six people were airlifted to hospital in serious condition.
The boat was found 39 nautical miles (72km) south of the island of El Hierro and was being towed to the port of La Estaca.
Separately, 84 survivors from another boat came ashore at La Restinga, El Hierro’s main port, which has a reception centre and field hospital for migrants.
The Canary Islands are a Spanish region in the Atlantic Ocean, off the coast of northwest Africa. Anyone who lands there reaches Spanish and European Union territory, which has made the islands a main entry point for migrants from West Africa.
Arrivals hit a record of more than 46,000 in 2024 before falling after tighter surveillance and cooperation with countries of origin and transit.
Patrols off Senegal, Mauritania and Morocco have pushed departures further south to The Gambia, Guinea-Bissau and Guinea, making the crossing longer and more dangerous.
Record arrivals
Arrivals in the Canary Islands have accelerated since October, with a record 2,100 people reaching the islands in a single day earlier this week, mostly on El Hierro, which has 11,400 residents.
Authorities there declared an emergency earlier this month, and rescuers brought in nearly 1,500 people in a single day on November 14.
“The humanitarian emergency doesn’t start on El Hierro, but on the shores of Senegal and Gambia, where we have to act,” regional leader Fernando Clavijo said on X.
He expressed “a lot of pain and feeling of impotence” over the deaths and demanded action from the Spanish government and the European Commission.
A campaign issue
The deaths come two days before Spain’s general elections on Sunday, in which immigration has become a defining issue.
Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is one of Europe’s most vocal advocates of the economic benefits of immigration, while the right, which leads in the polls, wants far tighter controls.
Thousands of migrants try the Atlantic crossing each year from West Africa in overcrowded boats, despite rough seas and strong currents.
It is one of the world’s deadliest migration routes, and arrivals usually rise between September and November, when sea conditions are more favourable.

items.text:
What went wrong for Chelsea as Xabi Alonso's side slip to new low following dismal defeat at Nottingham Forest
Sky Sports analyses the decisions from Xabi Alonso that contributed to Chelsea's 3-2 defeat to Nottingham Forest; Wesley Fofana started despite his controversial interview, while Levi Colwill was dropped; Xabi Alonso called for fundamentals but Chelsea were outrun
Saturday 28 November 2026 00:05, UK
Xabi Alonso called for his Chelsea side to get back to the fundamentals before kick-off - and then watched on as they were outworked and outclassed on their way to a miserable 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest.
"Everyone in the club and team, we need to stick together and go through this moment. We have to deal with it and we are responsible," Alonso told Sky Sports after the game, which marked their third successive defeat in the Premier League.
"It is a difficult moment for everyone at the club. For the team and the fans. Disappointed to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions.

"We can't stop. We are low in confidence. At this level you need to hold results and not concede so much. That is why we are losing."
Alonso now has as many losses in 15 games across all competitions as he did in 34 for Real Madrid (6). Since March, no side has more defeats in the top-flight than the Blues (14). And their problems are mounting by the day.
Here, Sky Sports analyses the decisions that contributed to the worrying defeat at the City Ground.
Chelsea failed at the fundamentals
Despite the calls from Alonso to strip the game back to basics and get the fundamentals right, Chelsea felt short from minute one.
At the half-time interval, facing a 1-0 deficit and with zero shots on target, Chelsea had ran 3.8km less than Oliver Glasner's side.
The Forest boss was then quick to point out that they had outrun their opponents by 6km after the game. Yes, Chelsea had more possession, but they were also well behind in high-speed runs.
"I've seen one team jogging after the ball and one team sprinting after the ball and in this day and age, you cannot do that," said Jamie Redknapp.
"Distance covered is not always the barometer, but one thing is for sure, high-speed runs will tell you everything."
Fofana in the firing line - should he have started?
Starting Wesley Fofana in the same week the player had to apologise for his controversial interview, where he said he can "laugh about" the penalty miss that contributed to their Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool and contemplated retirement during injury spells at the club, was a bold move from Alonso. It did not pay off.
The tone was set early on. Fofana's first touches were heavily booed by the travelling Chelsea fans who had made the 130-mile journey in the cold and rain to watch their side slip to yet another dismal defeat.
The centre-back could only watch on as Igor Jesus volleyed in his stunning opener but was at the centre of attention, for all the wrong reasons, for the second.
After misjudging the ball while battling with former teammate Liam Delap, who caused problems all evening, Fofana rushed to atone for his error and fouled the striker in the penalty area.
Morgan Gibbs-White doubled the lead from the spot and ultimately the comeback, led by substitute Emmanuel Emegha, fell short.
He was cautioned for the challenge and eventually taken off for Levi Colwill, who was dropped by Alonso instead of Fofana, and the fans booed him once again.
"It didn't feel like a game for him tonight. He had a bad week with the podcast," said Jamie Redknapp after the game.
"By playing Fofana tonight, you created that. It was inevitable. He is lacking so much confidence; he needs some time.
"He is having a real difficult run of it at the moment."
Caicedo at centre back - why?
After making the decision to drop Colwill, options at the centre of defence were limited with Maxence Lacroix and Reece James both sidelined.
Playing Josh Acheampong at centre-back and giving a rare start to Malo Gusto, an unused substitute on the night, seemed the more obvious choice but Alonso opted to play Moises Caicedo, arguably the best midfielder in the league, in the back four instead.
He was then tasked with dealing with a strike partnership of Delap and Igor Jesus. A difficult task for even the tallest of centre-backs, let alone a makeshift one standing at 5-foot-10.
He gave space to the Brazil striker for the opener and his presence in midfield was missed. He still led the way with 114 passes on the night, but Chelsea needed him in the middle of the park to deal with the likes of James McAtee and Xaver Schlager.
"They have bought players but if they do not sign a centre back, they cannot compete," said Redknapp after the game. He is right.
Emegha's impact was too little, too late
Alonso admitted that Emegha's performance after scoring twice off the bench was the lone positive for his side to take from their trip to the East Midlands. "For sure, he is having a good impact," he said. "He has done well. That is a positive."
He scored his first goal in the 4-1 defeat to Leeds United last time out but lost his place in the starting line-up on Friday.
Danny Welbeck, 36, was given the nod ahead of him and his performance mirrored the struggles Chelsea had as a unit.
Alonso called on the experience of Jordan Henderson and Welbeck to help weather their current struggles but it only whipped up the storm.
Welbeck was a bystander in the first half and had just seven touches before being replaced at the break, Emegha then scored with his first two to help spark hopes of a comeback.
His header for the second, holding off Jair Cunha, was one of the rare moments Chelsea matched the physicality of their opponents. He has to start moving forward without Joao Pedro available.

The Pittsburgh Steelers stun the Denver Broncos 27-5 in their first game since releasing four-time MVP quarterback Aaron Rodgers following his remarkable comments regarding
items.text:
NFL: Pittsburgh Steelers shock Denver Broncos 27-5 after Aaron Rodgers drama dominates build-up following Mike McCarthy claims
The Pittsburgh Steelers stun the Denver Broncos 27-5 in their first game since releasing four-time MVP quarterback Aaron Rodgers following his remarkable comments regarding head coach Mike McCarthy; Rodgers had accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings
Friday 27 November 2026 23:40, UK
It had been a week clouded by Aaron Rodgers and his explosive claims regarding head coach Mike McCarthy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers swatted at the storm to claim a shock 27-5 win over the Super Bowl-contending Denver Broncos on Black Friday.
Broncos quarterback Bo Nix endured a miserable afternoon as he surrendered two interceptions and a lost fumble that resulted in two defensive touchdowns for the Steelers.
Denver trailed 24-5 after a dire first half in which they were limited to just 58 yards of offense, becoming just the third team since 1991 to post fewer than 60 yards while conceding two defensive touchdowns over the first two quarters of a game.
TJ Watt scored with an end zone fumble recovery, Jalen Ramsey returned a Nix interception to the house and D.K. Metcalf recorded a touchdown catch before appearing to celebrate by holding up eight fingers in an apparent support of Rodgers.
The Broncos looked anything but a contender as they slumped to 8-3, while the Steelers distanced themselves from a reflection of turmoil to improve to 7-4 in their push for the playoffs.
- Bills beat Chiefs with field goal in final seconds
- Eagles sink Cowboys with historic Thanksgiving NFL comeback
- Get latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract
The Rodgers saga had lingered as an unwelcome backdrop heading into the game after the four-time MVP quarterback was released this week in the wake of his sensational appearance on the Pat McAfee Show.
Rodgers had claimed that head coach McCarthy fell asleep in team meetings, rebuffed suggestions to connect better with Pittsburgh's defensive players and accidentally shouted "one, two, three, Packers!" at the end of a team talk against the Philadelphia Eagles, the latter of which McCarthy would admit as an embarrassing moment.
Rodgers was subsequently cut amid what is set to mark the final season of his NFL career, though the storyline resurfaced during the game as broadcaster Al Michaels read a supposed text from the 42-year-old in which he is said to have claimed the Steelers had "barred" him from the team facility after he was benched for Mason Rudolph.
Rudolph started in place of Rodgers for the first time since the incident as he went nine of 15 passing for 142 yards and a touchdown, while Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren combined for 117 yards on the ground.
It took until 9.23 remaining in the third quarter for the first first down of the second half to arrive when the struggling Nix connected with Jaylen Waddle for 22 yards.
Still, it would come up empty amid a sequence of five successive punts between the teams, until Denver turned the ball over when Zach Allen forced a fumble from Dowdle that was recovered by Riley Moss with 3.31 on the clock.
Such was the story of their night that Denver failed to capitalise as their resulting drive ended in Wil Lutz missing a 53-yard field goal at the beginning of the fourth quarter.
Rudolph followed up by launching a downfield strike to Roman Wilson for 37 yards to set up Chris Boswell's 33-yard field goal for a 27-5 lead with 11.16 to play.
Nix's turnover issues resumed when he was intercepted by Daylen Everette at Pittsburgh's seven-yard line to ultimately end the game.
Stats leaders
Broncos
- Passing: Bo Nix, 22/40, 169 yards, 2 INTs
- Rushing: Cody Schrader, 7 carries, 27 yards
- Receiving: Jaylen Waddle, 5 catches, 53 yards
Steelers:
- Passing: Mason Rudolph, 9/15, 142 yards, 1 TD
- Rushing: Rico Dowdle, 11 carries, 71 yards
- Receiving: Germie Bernard, 1 catch, 58 yards
For so long defense has been the heartbeat of the Steelers operation, and it leapt to the occasion in the opening exchanges by way of TJ Watt as their stalwart edge rusher downed Nix's finger-slip fumble in the end zone for a deadlock-breaking touchdown in the first quarter.
Pittsburgh then forced a swift three-and-out to pave the way for Rudolph's 22-yard touchdown strike to Metcalf, who did outstandingly to haul in a back-pedalling catch while facing man coverage from star corner Pat Surtain II.
Denver turned to their own defense as a potential route back into the game when Alex Singleton stuffed Warren in the end zone for a safety, before Lutz and Boswell exchanged a pair of 44 and 47-yard field goals.
The Steelers then stretched their lead with a second defensive first-half touchdown when Ramsey turned a Nix interception into a 36-yard slaloming pick-six with 1.33 to play.

items.text:
US disables ship in Gulf of Oman under Iran blockade
November 28, 2026
The United States military on Friday announced it had fired at a ship in the Gulf of Oman that it said was violating Washington's blockade of Iranian ports.
A US aircraft fired "precision munitions" in the stern of the Palau-flagged Pacific Archer, US Central Command (CENTCOM), said, adding that it "continues to strictly enforce the [US] blockade."
CENTCOM oversees US forces in the Middle East.
The statement said that "the ship's propulsion was ultimately disabled" and stressed that "the civilian crew was unharmed."
It said that the ship had left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas.
The US blockade has disabled six ships and redirected 158 others.
Washington launched its blockade of Iranian ports in mid-July following the collapse of an agreement with Tehran.
The war broke out in February after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, which prompted Tehran to impose its own blockade on the Strait of Hormuz.
Kuwait summons Iran ambassador over strike on military site
Meanwhile, Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador after a Thursday drone strike killed two Italian technicians at a Kuwaiti military site.
A Kuwaiti citizen and a Pakistani citizen were also injured and hospitalized in the attack.
Iran has denied responsibility for the strike.
Kuwait's Foreign Ministry said Deputy Foreign Minister Hamad Al-Mashaan condemned the "continued Iranian attacks" and said Kuwait reserved its right to self-defense.
The two technicians worked for Rheinmetall Italia, a subsidiary of the German defense firm Rheinmetall.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the strike, calling on "all parties to exercise restraint."
Guterres is "deeply concerned by the continued escalation in the region," according to his spokesman, Stephane Dujarric. "Renewed hostilities would have devastating consequences for the region and beyond."

items.text:
Will Taiwan vote to revive nuclear power – and why does that matter for AI?
Voters will decide whether to scrap the country’s ‘nuclear-free homeland’ policy on Saturday.
Voters in Taiwan are set to decide whether to bring back nuclear power – 18 months after its last operational reactor was shut down.
A referendum on the issue is being held alongside local elections on Saturday. It is the island’s fourth vote on nuclear power in just eight years.
It comes as demand for electricity to fuel the country’s burgeoning computer chip industry soars and concern grows about how Taiwan would keep its lights on if China, which claims the island as its own territory, cut it off amid escalating tensions.
Here is what we know.
What is the referendum about?
Voters are being asked whether the government should return to using nuclear power to boost the economy. That would mean abolishing the country’s longstanding “nuclear-free homeland” policy.
The opposition Kuomintang (KMT) proposed the referendum and the Taiwan People’s Party (TPP) is also backing it. The legislature approved the referendum in August and the Central Election Commission signed it off on August 28.
To pass, ‘yes’ votes must outnumber ‘no’ votes and exceed a quarter of all eligible voters.
The ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), which has long had a policy of no nuclear power in its mandate, is urging ‘no’. DPP legislator Chen Pei-yu called the referendum unnecessary, saying lawmakers could change the policy by amending existing laws instead.
Why did Taiwan give up nuclear power?
Taiwan once relied heavily on nuclear power. In 1985, its three plants produced 52 percent of the nation’s electricity.
Nuclear power then became one of the most partisan issues in Taiwanese politics. Lev Nachman, an assistant professor at the Graduate Institute of National Development at National Taiwan University, said the divide goes back to the DPP’s founding.
“There was a major group of environmentalists that were part of the party that were very anti-nuclear,” Nachman told Al Jazeera. The nuclear industry, by contrast, was built and run under the KMT.
Polarisation turned that into “a very green-versus-blue issue”, Nachman said, referring to the colours of the DPP and the KMT.
Safety fears run deep. Nachman said Taiwan watched the 2011 Fukushima nuclear plant meltdown in neighbouring Japan very closely.
“There is this sort of fear of any sort of nuclear reaction that would ever happen in Taiwan would just devastate the entire island,” he said. Active geological fault lines run across Taiwan and the question of how to dispose of nuclear waste remains unresolved.
The DPP has governed since 2016, partly on a pledge to phase out nuclear power. In May last year, Taiwan shut down its last reactor at Maanshan in Pingtung County.
Why is nuclear power back on the agenda?
Public opinion has been mixed in three previous referendums. In 2018, voters opted to scrap a legal deadline for phasing out nuclear power. But in 2021, they rejected restarting construction on an unfinished fourth nuclear plant. In August last year, a majority vote to restart the Maanshan plant was voided due to low turnout.
Now, nuclear power is back on the agenda because surging electricity demand from Taiwan’s semiconductor and AI industries, along with growing fears about energy security and over-reliance on imported fuel, have renewed the debate over how the island keeps the lights on in an emergency.
According to the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan imports more than 97 percent of its energy. Natural gas generates about 43 percent of its electricity and coal about 35 percent. Both arrive by ship.
Taiwan only has about 11 days of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in reserve. Japan and South Korea hold between 14 and 20 days.
“There’s two sides to it,” Nachman said. The first is energy security: “If China actually blockades Taiwan and cuts off access to the outside world, then Taiwan only has so much energy it can rely on.”
The second is the chip industry, which requires huge amounts of power and “that’s only going to increase over time”, he said.
The war with Iran this year has added to the pressure by disrupting LNG shipments from the Middle East.
Will the ruling party change its stance?
The DPP has already started to shift. In March, President William Lai Ching-te said the government would begin the process of restarting the Maanshan and Kuosheng plants. He cited AI-driven demand and conflicts abroad causing disruption to energy supplies.
On September 24, the Nuclear Safety Commission approved state-owned Taipower’s restart plan for Maanshan. Further safety assessments are still needed before it can operate again.
Nachman said Lai has tried to push his party to rethink its “very dogmatic anti-nuclear stance”. The question is whether DPP voters have come around.
Nuclear power is not Taiwan’s first choice for filling the gap, however. “Investment in LNG – that’s still Taiwan’s kind of number one goal,” Nachman said.
How important is Taiwan’s microchip industry?
Taiwan is the most important link in the global AI supply chain.
It makes more than 90 percent of the world’s most advanced semiconductors, nearly all of them at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). TSMC has more than 60 percent of the global contract chipmaking market.
Its customers include Nvidia – the world’s most valuable semiconductor company – AMD and Apple. TSMC makes Nvidia’s Blackwell and Rubin AI processors, and Taiwanese firms such as Foxconn and Quanta build most of the world’s AI servers.
That uses huge amounts of electricity and water. In September, Taiwan’s semiconductor industry used more than 4.5 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity for the first time. That was up 11.55 percent from a year earlier, driven by AI demand.
S&P Global estimated that TSMC alone used about 8 percent of Taiwan’s electricity in 2023. That share could rise to almost 24 percent by 2030, it added.

items.summary:

We present DeepCrossAttention (DCA), an architecture that enhances transformer networks by using learnable weights and depth-wise cross-attention to dynamically combine outputs from previ
items.text:
November 23, 2026
Kyriakos Axiotis, Staff Research Scientist, and Thomas Fu, Principal Engineer, Google Research
We present DeepCrossAttention (DCA), an architecture that enhances transformer networks by using learnable weights and depth-wise cross-attention to dynamically combine outputs from previous layers, preventing the information dilution seen in traditional residual connections. Presented in our ICML 2025 paper, this architectural improvement allows models to achieve the same quality up to three times faster with a negligible increase in parameters.
Think of a traditional deep learning model like a giant game of "Telephone": data passes through layer after layer, with each layer changing the information slightly. If a network has dozens or hundreds of layers, the original learning signal can become severely degraded or lost by the time it reaches all layers, which is known as the vanishing gradient problem in AI.
To overcome this challenge and enable the training of networks with dozens or hundreds of layers, transformers rely heavily on residual connections, also known as “skip” connections, which act like an information highway or a shortcut. Instead of forcing the data to pass exclusively through the complicated layer, a duplicate copy of the original input skips right past this layer and is added directly to its output. This ensures that the model always has the original raw data to refer back to.
The standard residual connection implements a simple operation: point-wise summation of a layer's output with its input. While computationally efficient, this simple process has a key limitation: it treats all prior representations with equal weight, leading to information dilution in deep networks. As features propagate through many layers, specific, high-resolution details from earlier layers can be averaged out or distorted, making it difficult for the network to selectively retrieve them. This forces the network to recompute them, reducing learning efficiency.
In our ICML 2025 paper, "DeepCrossAttention: Supercharging Transformer Residual Connections," we studied the shortcomings of the traditional residual architecture and introduced DeepCrossAttention (DCA), which generalizes residual connections by allowing each layer to dynamically select and route features from the history of preceding layers. By allowing the model to dynamically choose which previous layers are most important at any given moment, DCA achieves comparable or improved learning, while reducing the number of parameters needed by up to 30-40%.
Instead of treating skip connections as a rigid, additive pipeline, DCA reframes residual learning as a dynamic routing problem. Rather than passing all prior layers forward with equal weight, DCA introduces a lightweight, layer-wise module that decides how to best combine previous embeddings on a per-token basis.
The architecture introduces two primary mechanisms:
- Dynamic layer routing: For every token processed, DCA computes a unique set of mixing weights using a static, learnable base combined with an input-dependent projection. This allows the network to adaptively shift its processing structure — ranging from purely sequential to fully parallel — based on the specific context of the token.
- Depth-wise cross-attention (split Q/K/V): While standard transformer attention operates across tokens in a sequence, DCA applies attention across layers in depth. Each token queries a dynamically weighted mix of all prior layer embeddings, unlocking the model's full historical context without the computational penalty usually required to scale traditional attention.
By allowing the network to dynamically select and retrieve high-resolution features from earlier layers, DCA eliminates the information dilution inherent to classic residual connections.
To test whether DCA can overcome information dilution in practice, we evaluated our approach across controlled synthetic setups, large-scale language modeling benchmarks, and image classification tasks.
DCA demonstrated significant improvements in convergence speed, training stability, and final model quality across these experiments.
On the colossal, cleaned version of Common Crawl's web crawl corpus (C4) and 1 Billion Word Language Model Benchmark (LM1B) datasets, DCA reached the performance of standard transformers in up to five times fewer training steps. When trained for the same duration or number of steps, DCA consistently achieved lower perplexity — how well a probability model predicts a sample — than standard residual connections, effectively extracting more representational capacity from the same training budget. To achieve a perplexity of <14 on LM1B, a standard transformer with fixed width required 42 layers, whereas the DCA model achieved a lower perplexity with only 30 layers — a 29% reduction in depth and parameter count.
One of the most common trade-offs in AI is that better models are often much larger and slower to run. DCA adds a tiny number of parameters — less than 0.2% of the total model size — making it negligible in terms of compute and memory footprint, while increasing memory bandwidth, as representations from different layers are presented intact rather than blended together. Interestingly, because DCA can be initialized to behave identically to a standard residual network, it doesn’t require training from scratch: retrofitting DCA onto an already pre-trained transformer and briefly continuing training reduced perplexity by 0.19 on LM1B, compared to just 0.02 for continued standard training.
As large language models (LLMs) are used across a broader range of domains, optimizing their training processes and underlying architectures is critical for scaling and unlocking new capabilities. DCA and similar dynamic residual techniques are already seeing significant adoption and success. The rapid emergence of these methodologies highlights dynamic routing as a highly active and promising area of research.
Develop

items.text:
Players Championship Finals: Gerwyn Price out in first round as Luke Humphries, Michael van Gerwen progress at Minehead
Report as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman all knocked out in first round at Players Championship Finals; watch the World Darts Championship at London's Alexandra Palace, live on Sky Sports from December 11-January 3
Friday 27 November 2026 23:46, UK
Three of darts' biggest names were subject to shock upsets in the Players Championship Finals as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman were all knocked out in the first round at Minehead.
Price was beaten by 6-4 Sebastian Bialecki - the first time the Pole had beaten the Welshman in his career - while Jeffery de Graaf won two legs on the bounce to consign van Veen to defeat by the same scoreline.
Nijman was upset by 20-year-old Henry Coates despite posting an average of 110 - the second-highest average in Players Championship Finals history.
- Players Championship Finals, day one - as it happened
- Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results
- Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW
World No 4 Luke Humphries, meanwhile, battled through his recurring back injury to secure a routine 6-3 victory against Darryl Pilgrim, while Michael van Gerwen withstood Connor Scutt to secure safe passage with a 6-3 first-round win of his own.
Beau Greaves also progressed to the second round with a scrappy 6-3 victory against former Lakeside champion Christian Kist despite a mediocre average of 89.64, and will face Rob Owen in the next round.
Van Veen, Nijman and Price joined James Wade, Gary Anderson, and Rob Cross as six of the top 25 players in the world were eliminated at the first opportunity in the last major before the World Darts Championship, which is live on Sky Sports from December 11th.
Wade was beaten 6-4 by Justin Hood and 2014 winner Anderson slipped to a 6-4 loss against Karel Sedlacek, while Cross fell to a thrilling 6-5 loss to Mickey Mansell.
Top players crumble on night of shock Minehead results
Van Veen - who finished runner-up to Price at the Grand Slam - struggled from the outset and throughout his match, managing only one maximum and checking out a lowly 15% of his finishes.
The Dutchman had three darts at double 16 to keep himself in the tournament, but failed to level the scores at 5-5 before de Graaf ruthlessly produced a 112 checkout to produce the first upset of the round.
Price, fresh off his first major win in four years after three successive final defeats, was heavily favoured against 22-year-old Bialecki, and looked to have rediscovered his tournament-winning form at the perfect moment when he produced a stunning 120 checkout to peg the deficit back to 5-4.
But Bialecki kept his cool and threw for the match, claiming his first career win against Price at the seventh attempt. The Pole will face off against de Graaf in round two.
The status quo was somewhat restored when Humphries and van Gerwen produced characteristically routine wins against lower-ranked opponents, with Humphries silencing doubters by averaging 93.32 in a week dominated by coverage of his injury.
But the show was stolen by Coates. The Derby native overcame his opponent's stellar average by notching an incredible 85.71% checkout success rate to claim victory in only his fourth-ever televised game.
Elsewhere, Stephen Bunting edged into the next round after beating German Max Hopp in a last-leg decider, while Kevin Doets averaged 107.34 in his win over Ritchie Edhouse and Chris Dobey came from behind to beat Mike De Decker 6-4.

items.title: Wilshere v Ramsey - Arsenal legends treading similar managerial paths

Wilshere v Ramsey - Arsenal legends treading similar managerial paths

items.text:
Wilshere v Ramsey - Arsenal legends treading similar managerial paths
- Published
Aaron Ramsey and Jack Wilshere have a lot in common.
Both were midfield prodigies. Both won the FA Cup playing for Arsenal under Arsene Wenger. Both represented their countries.
The image of the pair celebrating Ramsey's extra-time winner together in the 2014 FA Cup final against Hull City to end Arsenal's nine-year trophy drought at the time will forever be ingrained in the north London club's history.
They were teenagers when they made their Premier League debuts for the Gunners on the same day just two minutes apart as substitutes in a 4-0 win at Blackburn in September 2008.
Aged just 16 and 17, each were considered hot prospects who would go on to have excellent careers - and so it proved in many ways, even if both were restricted by injuries along the way.
Now 34 and 35, their paths cross again under different circumstances but many similarities very much still remain.
They are both in League One in their first permanent managerial jobs. And, guess what? Both their sides are in fine form and vying for promotion to the Championship.
It will be the first time they have met as permanent managers when Wilshere's Luton Town host Ramsey's Oxford United at Kenilworth Road on Saturday (15:00 GMT).
Ramsey and Wilshere have both tried to play down their reunion.
"Obviously it will be nice to see Jack again, but it's not about us," Ramsey told BBC Radio Oxford.
Except it is about them a little bit, given their 101 appearances in 10 years together in the Arsenal midfield - and as two young managers who are following almost identical paths.
Immediately after retiring from playing in July 2022, Wilshere was appointed the under-18s head coach at Arsenal, the club where he had risen from the youth academy to the first team.
Meanwhile, former Wales international Ramsey gained coaching experience towards the end of his playing career, also working with the under-18s at boyhood club Cardiff City.
Wilshere joined Norwich City as a coach for the 2024-25 season and it was at the end of that campaign he would first meet Ramsey as a manager in a remarkable twist of fate after they were both placed in interim charge of the Canaries and Bluebirds respectively.
The bragging rights went to Wilshere on that day in May last year as Norwich beat Cardiff 4-2.
"I owe him one from that," Ramsey joked.
Despite their close relationship and working towards the same objectives in the same league, they have not spoken "for a while".
"We are in a similar position at the moment, but I haven't had much dialogue with him over the last few months," said Ramsey.
"We're both fighting for the same things but, for me, it's just going out there to try and win a game of football."
Wilshere shared the same sentiment.
"It doesn't change anything for how we prepare," Wilshere told BBC Three Counties Radio on Friday.
"Of course, when I see Aaron, that'll be a nice moment. We spent a lot of good times together.
"He's had a really good start and credit to him. He's got a football brain, he's got a good career in the game and he's clearly taking that into his coaching.
"I wish him well, just not tomorrow."
Since taking over at Luton in October 2025, Wilshere has already tasted silverware, lifting the EFL Trophy at Wembley in April - a feeling he said he enjoyed more as a manager than when he was a player.
The 34-year-old guided the Hatters to seventh in League One last season, narrowly missing out on a play-off spot by a point.
Wilshere slightly edges his counterpart in terms of managerial experience, with 64 games in all competitions as Luton boss, while Ramsey has taken charge of 18 matches in his first season with the U's.
Neither could have their side in much better shape heading into Saturday's showdown.
After a stuttering start to 2026-27, Luton have won five of their past six games (D1) to climb from 16th up to fifth.
As for Ramsey, he is doing a fine job with Oxford considering the club have been under a transfer embargo since he arrived - and says he is "loving every second of it".
His side are on an 11-game unbeaten run - the second-longest across the entire Football League behind only Salford City (13).
With just one defeat so far, Oxford are third and three points behind Stockport and Huddersfield with two games in hand.
Students of Wenger and Arteta
The influences on Wilshere and Ramsey are clear to see, both in the styles of play they adopt and the way they conduct themselves.
They have both learnt from the same mentors, particularly Wenger and current Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, who they also played alongside in midfield.
It is perhaps no surprise the pair have gone into coaching - a common theme among Wenger's disciples.
Arteta, Patrick Vieira, Thierry Henry, Ashley Cole, Robin van Persie, Kolo Toure and Cesc Fabregas have also done so.
Wilshere and Ramsey have both spoken openly about the huge impact Wenger has had on them.
They also give a lot of credit to their role model Arteta.
Watching from afar, Ramsey previously said it was inspiring to see his former team-mate guide Arsenal to the Premier League title and Champions League final.
It was also Arteta who advised Ramsey to take his coaching badges and has continued to help him along the way.
But for Wilshere, he got to learn first hand from the Spaniard on the training ground.
"I got to see Mikel and how he coached and the influence he was having," Wilshere said last month.
"I would ask him questions, why he's doing certain things, and I started to fall in love with it and how he started to prepare training sessions.
"I was influenced by Mikel, but then I had to learn how to teach. I had to learn how to get that across, how to plan a session and how to get the outcomes that you wanted."
Forward-thinking and hard-working...

Sudan's lost generation: War is stealing the childhood of millions

SCOTT DETROW, HOST:
For millions of children in Sudan, classroo
items.text:
Sudan's lost generation: War is stealing the childhood of millions
Three years of war have stolen childhood from millions of children in Sudan, leaving them displaced, hungry and fighting for survival instead of learning in a classroom.
SCOTT DETROW, HOST:
For millions of children in Sudan, classrooms have been replaced by battlefields. Three years of civil war have left schools destroyed, families displaced and children exposed to drones, famine and forced marriage. Kate Bartlett reports.
(CROSSTALK)
KATE BARTLETT, BYLINE: The happy sounds of children playing belies their circumstances. These children are in a displacement camp in Tawila, in Sudan's North Darfur region.
SAM NUTT: If you ask the children how many of them were displaced by the war, every single hand goes up.
BARTLETT: Dr. Sam Nutt is the head of North American NGO War Child, which supports children in conflict zones with a particular focus on education. She's just returned from a trip to Sudan and described the capital Khartoum as, quote, "post-apocalyptic."
NUTT: If you ask the children one on one how many of them have witnessed someone who has been injured or killed as a result of the conflict, all of them say the same thing. Many of them lost one or both parents.
BARTLETT: Laura Mills from Amnesty International says this is just perpetuating the conflict.
LAURA MILLS: We spoke to many children in particular who told us that, you know, especially because they haven't been able to go to school for years, many of them saw their only option as going back to fight.
(SOUNDBITE OF EXPLOSIONS)
BARTLETT: The U.N. has called Sudan the world's worst humanitarian crisis. The conflict erupted in April 2023 when fighting broke out between Sudanese government troops and a paramilitary group called the Rapid Support Forces or RSF.
(SOUNDBITE OF EXPLOSIONS)
BARTLETT: Since then, the war has spread across the country, displacing millions and killing tens of thousands, according to the U.N. Both sides have committed atrocities, with the RSF accused of genocide in the remote western region of Darfur. And with almost 20 million Sudanese already facing acute hunger, U.N. agencies warn the super El Niño could exacerbate food shortages in the coming months. And while it might seem far away, the war in the strategically located mineral-rich country isn't happening in a vacuum, as Dr. Nutt explains.
NUTT: This conflict has significant global tentacles that are of interest to every single American.
BARTLETT: The conflict is not only impacting the surrounding countries, but is funded and supported by others much further away, from Iran and Russia to U.S. ally the United Arab Emirates, accused of backing the RSF, a charge it denies. Amnesty International's Mills again.
MILLS: Eventually, this is just going to lead to a more unstable world where we see the number of wars that are escalating by the day. And it will come back to haunt us.
BARTLETT: As for Sudan's children, there is one story in particular that has stayed with Dr. Nutt.
NUTT: There's one little girl who was 11-years-old in our class who wanted to be a doctor because she wanted to help keep people alive precisely because she had witnessed both of her parents being gunned down in front of her.
BARTLETT: The consequences of this war will also last long after the fighting stops.
Kate Bartlett, NPR News, Johannesburg.

items.summary:
