Nathan Lyon was left out of Australia's 13-player squad for their Test series against New Zealand on December 9 in Perth; Uncapped off-spinner Corey Rocchiccioli comes into the squad; Lyon was omitted from Australia's second
items.text:
Nathan Lyon dropped by Australia for their Test series against New Zealand
Nathan Lyon was left out of Australia's 13-player squad for their Test series against New Zealand on December 9 in Perth; Uncapped off-spinner Corey Rocchiccioli comes into the squad; Lyon was omitted from Australia's second Test vs South Africa
Friday 27 November 2026 22:54, UK
Nathan Lyon has been dropped by Australia for their upcoming Test series against New Zealand.
The 39-year-old off-spinner, who has been a mainstay for the Baggy Greens for 13 years, will be replaced by Western Australia's Corey Rocchiccioli.
Lyon has not spoken publicly since Usman Khawaja's explosive Sandpapergate claims were published in his autobiography.
- Sandpapergate forum to include 2017/18 Ashes series
- Sandpapergate explained as scandal re-enters the headlines
Australia selection chair George Bailey confirmed that his omission was not related to the ongoing saga, and was based on performances.
"Nathan has not quite had the impact we would like with the ball in recent matches," said Bailey.
"We also know he has an extraordinary record and his experience, knowledge and skill can still be valuable to the program we have moving forward."
Other notable omissions include Marnus Labuschagne, Cooper Connolly and Beau Webster, with middle-order batter Jack Clayton being drafted into the squad and is in line to make his debut during the series.
In recent years, Lyon has seen his role with the Test side diminished, with a right hamstring injury, sustained during day five of the third Ashes Test in 2025, ruling him out of Test selection for eight months.
Lyon, who ranks second as Australia's all-time leading wicket-taker behind Shane Warne with 577 wickets from 145 Tests, had previously been dropped for the second Ashes Test at The Gabba and spoke openly about the omission, saying he was "filthy" and "gutted" about being dropped.
Lyon had also been omitted from Australia's second Test against South Africa in October.
Prior to last year's Test at The Gabba, the off-spinner had remarkably not been left out of a Test squad since he made his debut in 2011.
Uncapped off-spinner Rocchiccioli will likely go head-to-head with Scott Boland for a spot in the side to play New Zealand on the fiery Perth pitch in the first Test which starts on December 9.
"Corey has been a strong performer in domestic cricket for the past few seasons and has traits that are well suited to Australian conditions," Bailey said.
Under-scrutiny skipper Pat Cummins will captain the side, while Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Steve Smith, who have all found themselves at the centre of Australia's recent Sandpapergate saga, were also named in the team.
Smith had missed Australia's final Test against South Africa in Cape Town with a neck injury.
Australia will add one final player after the sixth round of Sheffield Shield matches.
Australia squad to face New Zealand
Pat Cummins (c), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Jack Clayton, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Michael Neser, Matthew Renshaw, Corey Rocchiccioli, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc.
Australia Test series vs New Zealand
First Test: December 9-13, Perth Stadium
Second Test: December 17-21, Adelaide Oval
Third Test: December 26-30, MCG, Melbourne
Fourth Test: January 4-8, SCG, Sydney

items.title: Arteta sets Arsenal 100-point Premier League target to emulate Manchester City
items.summary:
Mikel Arteta has set Arsenal the target of emulating Manchester City by becoming only the second team in Premier League history to record 100 points in a season.
Arteta was an assistant for Pep Guardiola’s side when they achieved the landmark in the 2017-18 campaign, beating second-placed Manchester
items.text:
Mikel Arteta has set Arsenal the target of emulating Manchester City by becoming only the second team in Premier League history to record 100 points in a season.
Arteta was an assistant for Pep Guardiola’s side when they achieved the landmark in the 2017-18 campaign, beating second-placed Manchester United by 19 points. City head to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday already trailing Arsenal by six points after just 11 games, with Enzo Maresca’s side having failed to win any of their four previous league matches.
Arsenal drew against Newcastle last week and have only dropped points in one other game so far: a 3-0 defeat at Brighton in September. But Arteta said that his team will have to be exceptional if they are to match City’s record of only two defeats and four draws across the whole season.
“We haven’t hit the level yet that they did and I was there when we did 100 points,” he said. “That’s the level that is unprecedented and every record was beaten. That’s what we have to aim for because that’s what I expect that all the clubs and all the squads with the capacity they have in this league are going to aim for this season or the next few seasons.”
Asked if that City side was his benchmark as a manager, Arteta added: “You want to be the best version that you can. That’s something that’s been done only once in the league and that’s what we want to do. It’s going to be extremely difficult but we want to be as close as that because that’s what is going to increase the probability of winning the Championship again.”
City finished their record-breaking season in 2017-18 with a +79 goal difference and wrapped up the title with five games to spare. It also falls inside the nine-season period when they have been found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations. City have yet to learn their fate but Arteta denied that the uncertainty over what punishment they will receive could overshadow the game on Sunday.
“I hope that it doesn’t because this is a process that is still open and not resolved and I wouldn’t know what is going to happen,” he said. “I think when we have two teams at the level that they’re both in right now with the quality of play that they have on that pitch it’s a massive game and a big game to enjoy.”
Arteta also said retaining Arsenal’s title on the pitch is “the only thing that we should put the energy and the focus on”.
Arsenal supporters are being urged to arrive early on Sunday for a pre-match display. But Arteta bizarrely refused to comment on whether emotions will be running high among fans when City come to north London for the first time since being found guilty. “I don’t know. That’s something very individual and I don’t want to go there,” he said.
David Raya could play against City despite fears that the Spain goalkeeper could be out for a substantial period after injuring a shoulder against Newcastle last week. Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised against Borussia Dortmund in midweek and Arteta said he has full faith in the former Chelsea goalkeeper despite his error in the Carabao Cup final against City this year.
“The experience that Kepa has is already incredible. In the teams that he’s been involved [in], the squads that he’s been involved [in], the trophies that he’s won. There’s none of that [doubts],” he said.

The result left Spurs in the bottom three, two points below West Ha
items.text:
Tottenham’s trip to Sunderland takes Roberto De Zerbi back to the start. The Italian’s first game as the club’s manager came at the Stadium of Light in April and relegation was on the cards when his new side slipped to a 1-0 defeat.
The result left Spurs in the bottom three, two points below West Ham, and De Zerbi has not forgotten the reaction in the dressing room after the final whistle. Survival was secured on the final day of last season but he is taking nothing for granted after a promising run of form.
De Zerbi, whose side are six points off the top four after four wins in their last five games, remembers the mood seven months ago and plans to motivate his players before Sunday’s return to Sunderland by showing them footage of their devastation after their previous trip to the Stadium of Light.
“I am thinking of showing this video from the end of the game to the players tomorrow evening,” the manager said. “I want to start my meeting by speaking about that emotion on that day because I don’t want us to forget this moment. It is the key for my Tottenham. Maybe in the future with another coach this will change but my Tottenham was born that day.
“That day it was tough to accept the defeat, tough to accept the behaviour after the defeat but it was the crucial day. I have a great memory of the behaviour, even though we lost the game, because I understood better what we needed at the time. We didn’t need football. We didn’t need so many principles on the pitch. We needed completely different things.”
De Zerbi saw emotional baggage after the Sunderland game. “Too many people sad, many of them suffering too much, maybe too many people who didn’t believe enough in themselves, not enough smiles,” he said. “Now we have a good atmosphere, but we can’t forget. And we can’t be too happy with results because tomorrow you can lose again and become sad again.”
De Zerbi, who praised the club for persuading the 18-year-old winger Luca Williams-Barnett to sign a new contract, feels a good transfer window has put Spurs in a stronger position. “For the future I think we don’t need [signings] in too many positions,” he said. “I think we need to finish the squad in maybe three, four positions.”

items.title: US military says it disabled merchant ship trying to breach Iran blockade
items.summary:
US military says it disabled merchant ship trying to breach Iran blockade
The US military says it disabled the Palau-flagged ship’s propulsion but its crew was unharmed.
The US military says it has fired on a merchant vessel in the Gulf of Oman and claims it was trying to breach an American blockade
items.text:
US military says it disabled merchant ship trying to breach Iran blockade
The US military says it disabled the Palau-flagged ship’s propulsion but its crew was unharmed.
The US military says it has fired on a merchant vessel in the Gulf of Oman and claims it was trying to breach an American blockade on Iranian ports.
Military aircraft fired “precision munitions” at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer on Thursday, and the “ship’s propulsion was ultimately disabled and the civilian crew was unharmed”, US Central Command (CENTCOM) said in a statement.
US officials say the Pacific Archer left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas before it attempted to run the blockade. Ship tracking websites list the vessel’s destination as Singapore. It is at least the 15th vessel the US military has publicly acknowledged disabling since the blockade began in April, and the sixth since it resumed it in July. The previous vessel was disabled on November 7.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Friday that two tankers attempted to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an “unauthorised” route, claiming that one of them struck a naval mine while the other was forced to turn back.
The claims could not be independently verified.
The commander of the Iranian navy, Shahram Irani, said on Friday on state television that Iran will carry out operations “that will not only break the naval blockade but also drive the enemy out of the region’s waters”.
American blockade action
The US military has maintained a sizeable naval force in the region, including a constant presence of two aircraft carriers and a host of other ships.
American ships have been blockading Iranian ports since April, although the blockade was temporarily lifted during talks with Tehran and resumed in July. Since then, the US military says it has redirected 158 merchant ships and disabled those that refuse to comply.
CENTCOM, which has its headquarters in Florida, has consistently said that American forces issue multiple warnings before firing on the merchant ships.

items.title: Spygate tensions erupt at Southampton after Finn Azaz’s cry-baby celebration riles Boro
items.summary:
As Finn Azaz goaded the Middlesbrough supporters, pretending to cry in front of them after running the length of the pitch to deliver his mock crying celebration, Southampton’s fans hollered in the delight of what they perceived as something akin to justice or retribution.
Their Spygate crime has be
items.text:
As Finn Azaz goaded the Middlesbrough supporters, pretending to cry in front of them after running the length of the pitch to deliver his mock crying celebration, Southampton’s fans hollered in the delight of what they perceived as something akin to justice or retribution.
Their Spygate crime has been admitted, or embraced even, based on the behaviour of many associated with the south-coast club. But the sense of aggrievement that they were denied the chance of promotion last season remained. The fans felt it and the players certainly felt it. So when Azaz, a former Boro player, secured victory in this most heated of contests, adding a second goal to Ryan Manning’s opener, it was like a champagne cork had been unpopped.
In the buildup to the match, there had been a public desire from both managers to move on from events of last May that are now well known: the intern caught snooping on Middlesbrough training, Southampton’s subsequent expulsion from the Championship playoff final despite claiming victory on the pitch, and the five-month saga spent meting out full punishments.
Tonda Eckert had this week invited the Sky Sports cameras in for a well-timed, gentle PR piece revealing the man behind the scandal. His opposite number, Kim Hellberg, also attempted to put the matter to bed, revealing that the two managers chatted it through on a phone call and he would “never hold a grudge”.
So it was eye-catching, to say the least, when Southampton – and you would have to assume, given the importance of the subject matter, those at the very top – signed off release of an extraordinary video uploaded on to social media on Friday morning and then replayed pre-match on the big screens.
The clip, voiced by a local content creator, featured footage from both playoff semi-final legs, emphasising Southampton’s highs – “the night was ours” – and the lows – “until it wasn’t” – while carefully avoiding any specific reference to Spygate itself. It also, pointedly, showed Oli McBurnie wheeling away in celebration at Wembley after scoring the injury-time goal that sent Hull, and not Middlesbrough, to the Premier League. And it then, with a total absence of self-awareness, 55 seconds into a 79-second video spent looking backwards, delivered the farcical line: “People talk about last season. But we’re focused on this one.”
It all made for a febrile St Mary’s atmosphere, albeit there was a perfunctory feeling about the way both sets of supporters duly ran through their repertoire of chants – the away fans describing Southampton as “cheating bastards” and the hosts responding by suggesting “we’ll spy when we want”. The sideshow obscured the fact that there was plenty at stake beyond grudges, with Hellberg’s side arriving on the south coast top of the table and Southampton sitting only seven points behind, despite a four-point deduction.
It was January when Southampton fans last witnessed a home league defeat and, happily deploying the patient buildup that has become Eckert’s hallmark, the hosts came close to taking the lead a number of times in the first half. Lewis Dobbin stuck a free header wide, Azaz unleashed a piledriver against the Boro crossbar via Radek Vitek’s fingertips, and the Czech keeper then did well to keep out a firm Cyle Larin header. At the other end of an even contest, the Championship’s top scorer, Will Lankshear, twice spurned good chances.
If the opening period felt like a watchable dress rehearsal, what followed was the riveting main show. Soon after half-time, Lankshear was sent clean through on goal only for Keven Schlotterbeck to deny him with a brilliant last-ditch sliding tackle that clattered into ball and then ankle. As the two players squared up to one another, the occupants of both dugouts did the same.
The volume rose, fouls abounded and boiling point approached when the deadlock broke. An excellent referee’s advantage culminated in James Bree drilling the ball across the box where Manning poked it home. Cue delirium.
As tension continued to mount, a terrible defensive error presented Azaz with the ball inside the Boro penalty area, and he slotted home before embarking on his pitch-long celebratory venture. The melee that provoked was the first of many as emotions reached fever pitch. In all, 10 yellow cards were dished out – seven of them in the final half-hour. It was quite a watch.

items.title: Gibbs-White and Igor Jesus fire Nottingham Forest past shaky Chelsea
items.summary: Wesley Fofana, as a former Leicester City player, might have expected the celebrating Nottingham Forest fans to give him a hard time. But, at the end of a week in which he invited opprobrium by making light of missing a penalty at Liverpool in an unsanctioned French interview, he endured the ultimat
items.text:
Wesley Fofana, as a former Leicester City player, might have expected the celebrating Nottingham Forest fans to give him a hard time. But, at the end of a week in which he invited opprobrium by making light of missing a penalty at Liverpool in an unsanctioned French interview, he endured the ultimate ignominy when Chelsea supporters chanted foul-mouthed abuse at him, concluding: “You’re not welcome here.”
Fofana was humiliated by Liam Delap before fouling the former Chelsea striker to allow Morgan Gibbs-White to score a penalty for the first of his two goals that ultimately allowed Forest to follow their win over Manchester City to climb to 14th in the Premier League.
But even two goals for substitute Emmanuel Emegha, following on from his effort against Leeds, could not allow Xabi Alonso to smile after this fourth defeat in five games. There is clearly something rotten at the heart of Chelsea.
With the rain, fog and cold, an uncomfortable Friday night out in Nottingham soon became even more inhospitable for Chelsea. A rumbustious atmosphere was heightened when Forest went ahead with their first clear attack inside five minutes.
Liam Delap, with more than a point to prove, had already had one speculative 20-yarder on the turn saved by Emiliano Martínez after 62 seconds. Yet Chelsea, continuing their horrendous week, failed to heed the warning. When Jair Cunha nudged the ball wide to Daniel Muñoz, the right wing-back was given as much space to cross the ball as Igor Jesus was to swivel and plant his delicious right-foot volley into the top corner. It was a sumptuous goal, from the striker who also scored in Forest’s 3-1 win at Stamford Bridge in May, but the freedom he was given by the Chelsea defenders was baffling.
Xabi Alonso had elected to retain Fofana, despite the defender’s outrageously loose comments to a French YouTuber this week, and drop Levi Colwill, Moisés Caicedo retreating to the centre-back berth he adopted at Sunderland in emergency recently. With Forest bound to look to the physicality of Delap, it seemed a strange decision.
Andrew Madley, the referee, added flavour to this concoction by allowing Morgan Gibbs-White to shove Fofana off the ball with impunity, earning Forest a corner, then Caicedo to push Delap to the ground, again keeping the pea in his whistle dry. Chelsea gradually worked their way back into the game but without threatening more than a deflected shot from Roméo Lavia in the first half.
Forest were content to revert to a flat back five and ask Gibbs-White and Igor Jesus to work off Delap. Yet Chelsea, for all Alonso’s repeated insistence that he wants his team to press high, continuously allowed midfielders James McAtee and Xaver Schlager to have the ball as they came over halfway. It is not surprising to hear 15 teams came into this weekend having allowed opponents fewer passes per defensive action when observing this Chelsea showing.
Fofana’s decision to laugh at his shootout penalty miss in the EFL Cup defeat at Liverpool, and admit he had to be talked out of giving up football by his agent, in his unsanctioned interview this week has only worsened relations between Chelsea and their supporters. But then three defeats in their previous four Premier League games doesn’t exactly help. And playing with their precise, careful and blunt approach of the opening 45 minutes could have put the tin hat on things.
The night became even more embarrassing for Chelsea, and Fofana in particular, inside the first five minutes – again – of kick-off. The France defender misjudged a straightforward channel ball from James McAtee so that Delap got away from him. The former Chelsea striker knew he just had to get ahead of his man and either he would be able to get his shot away or his heels would be clipped. Fofana duly obliged; Gibbs-White converted the penalty.
The Chelsea fans in the Bridgford Stand compounded their player’s nightmare week with their abusive chants. Delap span away from his man with ease, Fofana knowing he could not risk fouling him from behind again. When Colwill, the substitute, prepared to come on, Chelsea’s No 3 had walked to the touchline before his number had even flashed up on the digital board. His humiliation was complete.
To the surprise of most in the ground, Chelsea came back into the game within three minutes of Gibbs-White’s penalty. Pedro Neto, who at least played with heart, surged across on to a one-two with Morgan Rogers to fire a shot goalwards that deflected off Cunha and fell for Emegha, on as a half-time substitute for Danny Welbeck, to score from close range. After his goal on his full Premier League debut against Leeds last week, perhaps this was something for Chelsea to build on.
The hope did not last long, however. Rogers, uncharacteristically, slashed wide when left free from Jordan Henderson’s corner. And when Gibbs-White timed his run on to Schlager’s brilliantly inventive pass to dink his third goal of the season over Martínez, Forest’s second successive home win looked assured. Chelsea’s dignity had long since been misplaced.

items.text:
Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law
- Published
Canadian prosecutors are seeking a 25-year prison sentence for a man who sold toxic chemicals through online suicide forums in 40 countries.
Kenneth Law pleaded guilty in May to 14 counts of aiding the suicide deaths of 14 people in Ontario, Canada, though he has admitted to causing the deaths of dozens of victims in England and Wales.
The 61-year-old will not face charges in the UK or over any British deaths under a plea deal which saw Canadian authorities withdraw more serious charges of murder.
During Friday's sentencing hearing in an Ontario court, prosecutors stressed that many of his victims were young and struggling with mental distress.
If Law receives the prosecution's recommended sentence, he would serve just under 20 years in prison, after accounting for credit for time served since his May 2023 arrest.
As she sought to make her case in court on Friday, Crown Attorney Kathleen Doherty described Law as a predator taking advantage of "vulnerable people".
"What they needed was help. But what they found was Mr Law and his products for death," Doherty said.
She also said Law's motives were financial.
"If people could pay, he sold it to them. There's no discussion or inquiries or anything going on whereby Mr Law would have any ability to appreciate the circumstances of the individual he was dealing with," she said.
Law's defence lawyer, Matthew Gourlay, countered those claims, arguing that his client was not responsible for many of their battles with mental illness.
He said Law held a "misguided belief" he was helping his victims.
"Each of these incidents is its own unique tragedy," Gourlay said. "Mr Law may be a common denominator between them, but Mr Law was not the cause of the struggles and hardships that caused all these victims to seek out his products in the first place."
Law's defence attorney has asked the court to give him a 12-year sentence.
The sentencing hearing on Friday followed an emotional few days of testimony in September, when grieving family members and friends told the court of the pain Law had caused.
Those impact statements will be taken into account at sentencing, which is due at a later date.
Authorities said the former chef sold about 1,200 packages of toxic substances to recipients - who he met in online suicide forums - in 40 countries, roughly a quarter of which were sent to the UK.

items.text:
S&P revises France's outlook from 'stable' to 'negative'
Rating agency S&P revised France’s outlook to "negative" from "stable" on Friday, citing growing budget pressures as weak economic growth and higher interest costs make it harder to reduce the deficit.
S&P Global Ratings on Friday confirmed France’s sovereign rating at A+/A-1, but assigned it a negative outlook, raising the threat of a further downgrade in the medium term.
The US agency attributed its decision to “the increase in public debt against a backdrop of moderate economic growth prospects”, as the French economy entered a technical recession, according to figures released Friday by France's official statistics bureau INSEE.
Emphasising the “need for fiscal consolidation”, S&P also pointed to “the high risk that political fragmentation will persist after the 2027 presidential election,” which will weigh on economic growth.
The agency said it expects France’s public debt to continue to rise next year and for the interest paid by Paris to its creditors to increase gradually between now and 2029.
(FRANCE 24 with Reuters)

Friday 27 November 2026 21:57, UK
Southampton's unbeaten start to the season at St Mary's continued as they beat leaders Middlesbrough 2-0.
Six-and-a-half months on from 'Spygate' - which dominated the headlines during last season's play-offs - Saints emerged victorious, as they did in the semi-final second leg, in an ill-tempered affair that saw 10 yellow cards brandished to players and two to coaching staff.
Had it not been for the four-point penalty imposed on them as a result, Friday night's win would have sent them to the top of the Sky Bet Championship.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats
- Watch FREE Championship highlights | Latest EFL news and rumours
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream EFL games with no contract📺
But goals from Ryan Manning and Finn Azaz - who goaded his former club's fans as he celebrated - put them within touching distance of the summit.
Boro's third defeat of the season opens the door to Stoke and Wolves to leapfrog them into top spot if they win on Saturday.
In the build-up, Tonda Eckert and Kim Hellberg insisted they had buried the hatchet - but neither fanbase had forgotten it. Both sets of players were booed when they came out to warm up, while chants referencing the saga echoed around St Mary's. The atmosphere was electric.
Meaningful chances came at a premium in the first half, but they were high quality when they did come.
The home fans fell silent for a split-second when Will Lankshear ghosted away from his man and moved one-on-one with Saints goalkeeper Daniel Peretz, who denied the Championship's top scorer.
And at the other end, Radek Vitek had to be at his best, first to tip Azaz's fierce strike onto the crossbar, then to push a Cyle Larin header over.
The first goal came just before the hour. Kuryu Matsuki's cross flew over everyone in the box, but James Bree was there to collect and fizz in a low ball that Manning ran onto and side-footed high into the net.
Twenty minutes later, Azaz capitalised on a defensive mistake to calmly slot home the second, before running straight towards the visiting supporters and making a sarcastic crying gesture, sparking a heated reaction.
This is not a rivalry that is going anywhere any time soon.
Azaz explains celebration - and has no regrets over it...
Southampton's Finn Azaz speaking to Sky Sports:
"They sang about my family home and away last season, so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back.
No regrets then? "None whatsoever."

items.text:
Gibbs-White stars, Fofana struggles - player ratings for Forest v Chelsea
- Published
Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice as Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea at the City Ground for the first time since 1997.
Igor Jesus' brilliant volley opened the scoring after just five minutes, before Gibbs-White struck twice in the second half as Chelsea were consigned to a fourth defeat in five matches.
Forest ran out 3-2 winners despite Emmanuel Emegha twice pulling goals back.
Here's how I rated the players and how you rated the players.
- What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean? 
  - Published21 August
Nottingham Forest
Matz Sels: The Belgian goalkeeper could do little about Emegha's goal but did not need to make many saves. 6
Jair Cunha: Cunha made one brilliant last-ditch tackle in the second half as Chelsea pushed for an equaliser. 7
Nikola Milenkovic: The Serbian was solid in the middle of the back three but otherwise unremarkable. 7
Murillo: The Brazilian centre-back made a host of important tackles and no-nonsense clearances throughout. He set the tone for a physical display and had a powerful volley saved. 7
Daniel Munoz: A typically energetic presence on the right, he also set up the opening goal. 7
James McAtee: The midfielder was good in possession but his shots lacked threat. His set-piece delivery was also poor. He did, however, win a few fouls for his team to take the pressure off. 7
Xaver Schlager: The combative midfielder set the tone early by winning the ball back in Chelsea's half on multiple occasions. He screened the backline well as Chelsea pushed for an equaliser. His wonderful pass through the eye of the needle created Forest's third. 9
Neco Williams: The Welshman battled hard with Pedro Neto in a tactical contest that ended with both players emerging with credit. 7
Igor Jesus: His sensational first-time volley opened the scoring just five minutes into the match, while the rest of his play was neat and tidy. 8
Morgan Gibbs-White: The forward scored his first goal in 11 games against Chelsea from the penalty spot in the second half. He took that chance and then another when played through by Schlager. 8
Liam Delap: The former Chelsea striker proved his worth to Forest by leading the line brilliantly, carrying a threat, looking dangerous in transition and ultimately winning a penalty for his side. 8
Subs:
Dan Ndoye (on 71, Jesus)
Ibrahim Sangare (on 84, Schlager)
Chris Wood (on 84, Delap)
Subs not used: John Victor, Netz, Diomande, Yates, Hudson-Odoi, Kalimuendo
Chelsea
Emiliano Martinez: The Argentine goalkeeper was sent the wrong way from the spot and could not have saved Jesus' volley but made a couple of other saves. 6
Josh Acheampong: The young defender played within himself at the City Ground. 5
Wesley Fofana: The Frenchman was booed by his own supporters and told he is "not welcome here". It was a tough end to a horrible week which only got worse as he gave away the penalty having first been caught under a long ball. He was substituted in the 56th minute while also on a yellow card. 3
Moises Caicedo: A shock selection to start at centre-back for first time in his 210 games in English football, the Ecuadorian looked out of sorts with possession and in his positioning. He failed to cover for Fofana before he gave away the penalty. 5
Pep Chavarria: The Spanish full-back was an anonymous presence but did not make any obvious mistakes. 5
Romeo Lavia: The Belgian recovered from a poor touch early on to set the tempo for possession domination and his passes had real purpose. 7
Jordan Henderson: The 36-year-old was one of the weaker Chelsea performers as he filled in for now-defender Caicedo. 5
Pedro Neto: The Portuguese winger showed impressive work-rate competing with Williams, while threatened with his running in behind. His second-half shot was blocked but led to Chelsea's goal, while his cross set up his side's second. 7
Cole Palmer: The forward was creative and highly involved for Chelsea but could not deliver that moment. It owed more to his team-mates not performing than himself. 6
Morgan Rogers: Rogers squandered multiple chances, including a huge opportunity to equalise from a corner midway through the second half. 4
Danny Welbeck: The 35-year-old striker had absolutely no service but was also completely anonymous in the first half and was taken off at the interval. 4
Subs:
Emmanuel Emegha (on 45, Welbeck): An outstanding second-half display, with a brilliant touch and shot to pull one after the ball deflected into his path. He headed in a second at the far post. It raises the question about why he did not start having also scored against Leeds last weekend. 8
Levi Colwill (on 56, Fofana): The England international will be frustrated to have been dropped for a midfielder but was forced on amid Fofana's struggles and did not have much chance to shine. 5
Geovany Quenda (on 85, Henderson)
Marco Palestra (on 85, Acheampong)
Subs not used: Penders, Gusto, Barco, Nicoll-Jazuli, Estevao

A Green Brigade stateme
items.text:
Celtic defend head of security amid Green Brigade row
- Published
Celtic have defended their head of security and the action taken against the Green Brigade last season after the fan group declared four supporters had been cleared over the incident that sparked a lengthy ban.
A Green Brigade statement said the four had been "finally cleared of wrongdoing" over the occurrence, which took place during a game against Falkirk on 29 October last year.
The Scottish champions released footage at the time which they said showed "around 100" supporters verbally abusing and assaulting a steward and two police officers.
The alleged flashpoint came after a ticket inspection at the rail seating section of Celtic Park, the club explained, as they outlined a ban on about 250 supporters, which lasted nearly six months.
The Green Brigade say Celtic's "irresponsible and vindictive claim" was intended to "smear" them.
A statement from the group said: "Not guilty pleas were accepted by both Procurator Fiscal and sheriff for breach of the peace charges before the trial commenced.
"The four supporters cleared were subjected to dawn raids, damage to homes and harassment of family members including confiscation of personal devices, this included a vulnerable adult who was left alone in the cold with no means to contact anyone after the front door was removed."
- Celtic lift suspension of Green Brigade fans group 
  - Published7 April
The Green Brigade called for the club to apologise for the collective ban and to lift suspensions on two supporters who remain banned over their interaction with head of security Mark Hargreaves at last year's abandoned annual general meeting.
"This week's outcome represents significant vindication for all supporters concerned in these events over the past year," they added.
"It also calls into question the credibility of Mark Hargreaves' subsequent allegations against two Green Brigade representatives.
"We maintain that Mark Hargreaves has introduced a poisonous security culture to Celtic Park and does not hold the trust of supporters whose safety he is supposed to be responsible for. His position is untenable."
Celtic pointed out they play no part in criminal proceedings and added that they were not aware all had been completed. And they stated that the outcome of the four cases did not alter their assessment of the incident.
The club said: "The conduct of the group witnessed that day was unsafe and completely unacceptable – it has no place at Celtic Park or anywhere in football. The club took reasonable and proportionate steps to deal with this conduct.
"Such was the seriousness of the incident that the club was called to attend a special meeting of the Safety Advisory Group of Glasgow City Council."
Celtic accused the Green Brigade of continuing a "campaign of personal harassment and abuse" towards former senior police officer Hargreaves.
"Mark is a highly-qualified, dedicated professional who plays a crucial role at the club in ensuring the safety of our supporters.
"Where conduct presents an unacceptable risk to that safety or demonstrates an unwillingness to co-operate with it, the club has to take appropriate and proportionate action."

Report and free match highlights as Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea 3-2 at The City Ground; Igor Jesus opened the scoring before Morgan Gibbs-White scored two. Emmanuel Emegha's brace in vain; Wesley Fofana was booed by the Chelsea supporters
Friday 27 November 2026 22:16, UK
Morgan Gibbs-White scored two in Nottingham Forest’s 3-2 win over Chelsea at the City Ground as the crisis deepened for Xabi Alonso.
Igor Jesus volleyed Forest in front inside five minutes of what was a dismal first half for Chelsea and they never recovered parity. Wesley Fofana - booed by his own supporters throughout - conceded a penalty early in the second half that Gibbs-White converted.
Emmanuel Emegha did come off the bench to pull one back soon afterwards but another goal from the Forest captain better reflected the superiority of Oliver Glasner's side even if Emegha's second in the 89th minute made for a surprisingly nervy finale.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats
- Live Premier League table | Watch FREE PL highlights
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract on NOW 📺
Forest began the evening beside the Trent with only goal difference keeping them out of the relegation zone, but victory lifts them clear of the bottom six. The spotlight now falls on Chelsea, who missed the chance to climb back into the top five.
It is four Premier League defeats in their last five games under Alonso who appears to be scrambling for solutions given the evidence of this team selection. It is not only Fofana under scrutiny at Chelsea. A club in disarray? Alonso needs to get a grip on it and fast.
How Forest were too good for Chelsea
Liam Delap had been the two-goal hero in the 3-1 win over Manchester City last time out at home and would have been desperate to score against another of his former clubs but it was Igor Jesus' stunning strike that silenced the Chelsea supporters early on.
"It is the first opportunity for them to play together, they have different strengths," Glasner had told Sky Sports beforehand. Igor Jesus' strengths include volleys beyond Emiliano Martinez, it turns out. It was his first goal at the City Ground since April.
Alonso had responded to the alarming defeat to Leeds by dropping Levi Colwill and playing Moises Caicedo in defence. The Chelsea boss changed to a back four as well in a bid to find some form after losing three of their previous four Premier League games.
"Today we need strong characters, big personalities," said Alonso beforehand. "Players that know what it takes to compete in the Premier League." That explained the decision to bring in Danny Welbeck up front, with Jordan Henderson holding midfield together.
But Welbeck was a passenger in the first half, having only seven touches of the ball - half as many as anyone else - while Henderson found himself overrun. Forest were at the back line time and again. Chelsea were fortunate to be only one down at the break.
Fofana had not endeared himself to supporters by giving an unauthorised interview in which he not only talked of being close to quitting football but appeared to joke about missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool. This performance was worse.
He was culpable for Forest's second goal, bested by Delap before hastily fouling him inside the penalty box in a rash attempt to recover. Gibbs-White slotted home from the spot and Fofana was substituted to the sound obscene chants from the Chelsea fans.
Alonso's side did pull one back through the young substitute Emegha, when Pedro Neto's shot was deflected kindly into his path. But Xaver Schlager's sumptuous ball clipped in behind the Chelsea defence allowed Gibbs-White to hook home his second.
Emegha nodded in another late on to make the decision to omit him after scoring the first goal against Leeds look even more of an error, but it was not enough to earn an undeserved point. Forest held on and are on the up again. Chelsea have problems.
The key moments from The City Ground
5 - GOAL! Igor Jesus volleyed Forest into an early lead
51 - GOAL! Gibbs-White doubled the lead from the spot
54 - GOAL! Substitute Emegha pulled one goal back
73 - GOAL! Gibbs-White latched onto Schlager's pass
89 - GOAL! Emegha scored his second of the night
Alonso: Things are not clicking
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso speaking in the press conference:
"We are working, trying to find solutions, trying to do our best, but things are not going the way we want. And I don't understand any other way but to work, to try again.
"Because if we want to get something, it will have to come from us. No one will come from outside to give us a solution. And the quality that we need, the mentality that we need, it needs to come from within the team.
"Overall, we can do better. I think that we are going through a difficult moment of confidence, things are not clicking, things are not going the way we want.
"We know that in football, this can change quickly, or this can continue. So it's down to us to work and to find solutions to have a better feeling on the pitch and to get better results, because that's what we need."
Asked if he was frustrated with the Chelsea fans booing Wesley Fofana:
"We need to support everyone because we need everyone. We need the fans, we need all the players, we need to stick together, because if not, it will get more complicated."

The jeers aimed at the 25-year-old were heard every
items.text:
'You're not welcome here' - Chelsea's Fofana booed by own fans
- Published
Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana was subjected to repeated boos and told "you're not welcome here" by his own fans during Friday's Premier League defeat by Nottingham Forest.
The jeers aimed at the 25-year-old were heard every time he touched the ball and came after an unauthorised interview with French YouTuber Zach Nani was released.
In that controversial two-hour conversation, Fofana also appeared to joke about missing his penalty during last month's Carabao Cup shootout defeat by Liverpool.
Manager Xabi Alonso said the French centre-back had apologised and "it won't be repeated".
But Fofana endured a difficult time in his side's trip to Forest as supporters made their feelings known.
After Chelsea went behind to a brilliant volley from Igor Jesus in the fifth minute, Fofana also conceded a penalty for the home side's second goal from Morgan Gibbs-White in the 51st minute.
He was booked for the foul on Liam Delap in the box, and then replaced by Levi Colwill in the 56th minute - just after Emmanuel Emegha had pulled a goal back for the visitors - before Gibbs-White made it 3-1 in the 72nd minute.
Emegha scored again in the 89th minute to make it 3-2, but Forest held on to secure their first win over Chelsea at the City Ground since 1997.
Meanwhile, Nani has moved to defend Fofana, saying the player was "clearly" not happy during the interview and admitted he had to perform better.
Fofana also explained he opted to take a penalty against Liverpool as one of the senior players on the pitch, having joined in a £75m move from Leicester City in 2022.
But he confessed football had reached a stage where he was "more unhappy than happy", before recovering physically and mentally.
The release of the interview has coincided with the club's poor run of form, with Chelsea losing 4-1 at home to Leeds United last weekend to make it three defeats in four matches.
The defence, in particular, has come in for criticism, with the Blues one of four clubs to have conceded more than 20 goals in the Premier League after 11 matches.
Having been subjected to racist abuse in the past, Fofana spoke about handling comments during a club-organised interview on this summer's pre-season tour of Asia.
He is understood to be one of the highest earners at Stamford Bridge.

items.title: Why are families going hungry in northern Yemen even where food is on sale?
items.summary:
Why are families going hungry in northern Yemen even where food is on sale?
Flour and oil still reach markets in Hodeidah and Sanaa. But rising costs, scarce work and loss of food aid put them out of reach.
Umm Sami, a widow raising four children in Yemen’s Red Sea port city of Hodeidah, sells house
items.text:
Why are families going hungry in northern Yemen even where food is on sale?
Flour and oil still reach markets in Hodeidah and Sanaa. But rising costs, scarce work and loss of food aid put them out of reach.
Umm Sami, a widow raising four children in Yemen’s Red Sea port city of Hodeidah, sells household goods and takes on occasional domestic work to feed her family. Rising prices have changed how she shops. “Sometimes we buy a little flour or oil that lasts just one day because we cannot afford a whole bag,” she told Al Jazeera.
Food is still on the shelves. It was available in the markets that monitors could reach in September, but families had less money to spend, according to the Yemen Joint Monitoring Report, a humanitarian and food security assessment. Across Houthi-controlled areas like Hodeidah, a basket of basic foods cost about 7 percent, or $91, more that month than in August, its highest level in a year.
Families on both sides of the front lines are struggling, and prices are rising faster in the government-held south, according to the Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET). What sets the Houthi-controlled north apart is how little families there can earn and how little help is left.
Most households in and around northern towns find only five to 10 days of paid work a month, FEWS NET reported in October. The UN World Food Programme’s (WFP) food assistance in Houthi-held areas has been suspended since September 2025, FEWS NET said. By mid-September 2026, WFP had begun a distribution round in government-held areas that aimed to reach about 1.7 million people.
In the last nationwide hunger analysis by UN agencies and their partners, published in mid-2025, the only people projected to face catastrophic hunger, about 41,000, were in four districts of Amran, Hodeidah and Hajjah governorates – all under Houthi control.
On Friday, the WFP and the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) named Yemen among its hunger hotspots of highest concern for the six months ending May 2027.
As fighting spreads and aid dries up, we look at why food on sale in northern Yemen is slipping out of reach of the families who need it.
Why are some families in Hodeidah buying food one day at a time?
Because a day’s work – when there is any – no longer pays for a day’s food.
Ahmed Arjash drives a rented motorcycle taxi near Hodeidah’s Othman market to support his family of six. Many of his former customers now walk to save the fare. “Now, my daily earnings barely cover the fuel or the rent for the motorcycle,” he told Al Jazeera.
Saleh, a construction worker paid by the day, said some days pass without anyone hiring him. “If I work one day, the wage is not enough to cover the family’s needs for several days with prices this high,” he said.
Fishing pays less, too. Salem, a fisherman in his 30s, said fuel, boats and equipment cost him more while fewer customers could afford his catch. “Many families no longer buy fish as they used to,” he said. On some trips, he barely earns back what it costs to go to sea.
Families are adjusting by eating less. In Hodeidah’s poorest neighbourhoods, many skip meals or go without meat, fish, milk and fruit, Al Jazeera found.
In Houthi-held areas, FEWS NET reported that higher taxes on street vendors and shops had already reduced demand for labour in September. In its outlook through May 2027, it expected more small businesses to close and those that stayed open to hire fewer workers.
How does food reach shops in northern Yemen, and what makes the journey more expensive?
Almost all of it comes by sea, and each step from ship to shop now costs more. Yemen imports about 90 percent of its food, according to WFP. Hodeidah is the main port supplying the Houthi-held north, including Sanaa.
Food has kept arriving – data shows imports into Houthi-held areas rose 10 percent between June and August compared with the previous three months and doubled year-on-year – but fuel has not.
Fuel imports fell about 85 percent year-on-year in August, with no recorded arrivals of diesel or petrol through northern ports, according to the FAO. In September, the Houthi authorities raised the price of petrol by about 10 percent, the first increase in four years, Al Jazeera reported. Bread prices in Houthi-held areas rose 25 percent that month, FEWS NET said.
The ports themselves have come under attack. On November 2, the Houthi-run Al Masirah TV said Saudi aircraft had hit a pier and a commercial ship at Ras Isa port, north of Hodeidah, the news agency AFP reported. On Tuesday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had attacked “operational capabilities” in Hodeidah, and the Houthis threatened to retaliate against Saudi Red Sea ports. Hodeidah port remains open, Al Jazeera reported. How the latest attacks will affect deliveries remains unclear.
Moving goods inland has also become slower and costlier. A truck travelling between the south and the north “now takes up to a week to reach its final destination”, Saleh Abdullah, a shopkeeper in Sanaa, told Al Jazeera in September. Before the renewed fighting, the trip took three days or less. Customers pay the extra transport and fuel costs, he said. “Whether it is the flour, the baby milk, the fruits, the vegetables, or anything else.”
When families cannot afford food, what stops aid from reaching them?
In the north, the main source of food aid has been switched off. WFP suspended its activities in Houthi-controlled areas in September 2025 after the group detained UN staff. Last month, WFP said 73 UN personnel, 38 of them its own staff, remained in detention.
Other aid organisations still operate in the north, but funding cuts and restrictions limit their reach.
On Thursday, the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) said a handful of overstretched and underfunded Yemeni and international organisations were the only remaining lifeline for millions there.
Funding cuts, sanctions and the UN’s pause in operations had all contributed to a collapsing humanitarian res

items.text:
Ukraine submits Black Sea ceasefire offer, awaits Russian response
Ukraine made a Black Sea ceasefire offer to enable food exports and passed the details on to international allies, a senior Ukrainian official said Friday, adding that Kyiv was waiting for a response from Moscow. The announcement came a day after Russia attacked two foreign grain carriers near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, according to Ukrainian authorities.
Ukraine has offered a Black Sea ceasefire to enable food exports and passed this on to international allies, Kyiv's ‌foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said on Friday.
"We are ‌ready for a ceasefire. We are grateful to India, Turkey, and Egypt, which are playing an active ‌and important role in de-escalating tensions in the Black ‌Sea, as well as in mediation efforts. We are now awaiting a response from Russia," Sybiha was cited by Suspilne public broadcaster.
He added that Russia had proposed Ukraine suspend attacks on the Russian oil sector under the truce, but Kyiv would only consider this as part of a bigger energy ceasefire deal.
Speaking at the 5th International Food From Ukraine Conference, Sybiha said that while Kyiv had presented its partners with clear Black Sea ceasefire proposals, Russia was trying to include oil supplies among the conditions related to agricultural products, Ukrainian news agency RBC-Ukraine reported.
The announcement came a day after Russia attacked two foreign cargo ships carrying more than 100,000 metric tons of grain overnight near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, according to Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergiy Koretskyi.
He did not say where the grain originated nor where the ‌vessels had loaded their cargo.
Ukraine has said grain shipments from its key Black Sea ports around Odesa have all but stopped ‌since late July after Russia sharply intensified attacks on grain terminals and merchant vessels.
Russia says it does not attack civilian targets.
Before the escalation, the three ports in the Odesa hub handled about 90 percent of Ukraine's agricultural and metallurgical exports.
Kyiv ‌has not formally banned port operations, but shipowners have avoided the ports because of security risks, while soaring insurance costs have deterred traders.
At an APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, last week, Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would no longer consider a moratorium on strikes in the Black Sea or on energy infrastructure following Ukraine's ‌attacks on the bridge linking Russia and Crimea.
Putin's threat came shortly after Kyiv struck the Kerch Strait Bridge for ‌the third time in a week, damaging a route long used by Moscow to move men and materiel into Crimea and the southern front.
Read moreWhy Ukraine keeps trying to bring down Russia's bridge to Crimea
Frustration over Trump's 'strange' friendship
Meanwhile Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Friday expressed frustration with the US stance toward Putin, in the latest sign of deepening tension between Kyiv and Washington, as new questions emerged about Europe’s future financial commitments to Ukraine.
Zelensky said in an interview with the BBC broadcast Friday that he wants the US to apply more pressure on Putin to stop his invasion of Ukraine, which began almost five years ago and grinds on despite President Donald Trump’s efforts to broker a peace deal.
The Ukrainian president described Trump calling Putin “my friend” at a recent summit in China as “strange” because the Russian leader is “an aggressor and a killer”.
“He can’t be a friend,” Zelensky told the British broadcaster in Kyiv, likening the statement to someone calling Adolf Hitler a friend during World War II.

The White House did not respond to a request for comment on Zelensky’s remarks. But Trump on Thursday defended his reference to Putin. “We want to make a deal. We want to stop the killing,” he said.
“I could walk in and say, ‘I don’t like you!’ and then we have the same problem that we have with Zelensky and Putin,” he said. Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago, he added: “The biggest problem with that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other.”
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Zelensky was “insulting his counterpart”, showing that the Ukrainian leader “is not willing to follow the path of (a) peace settlement”.
The International Criminal Court has issued an arrest warrant for Putin for war crimes, accusing him of personal responsibility for the abductions of children from Ukraine. The Trump administration has imposed sweeping sanctions on the court as part of its campaign to dismantle the tribunal over investigations into the US and its allies, including Israel.
The Kremlin has said that Russia also does not recognise the ICC and considers its decisions “legally void”. Peskov in 2023 called the court’s move against Putin “outrageous and unacceptable”.
Kids return from Russia and Russian-occupied territories
Nine Ukrainian children were returned Friday from Russia and Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine, including an 8-year-old boy who ran out of a bus as it pulled up at Ukraine’s northern border in the Chernihiv region.
“Mom!” he shouted into the crowd. His mother, Alina Sydorenko, was there to reunite with him after nearly five years apart.
She hugged him tight as he kept saying, “Mother, mother.”
“I want to show him everything that he missed and was taken away from him,” Sydorenko said.
Some of the children had lost their parents, who died in occupied territory. Relatives met them at the bus.

Spain's main party leaders have held their final rallies ahead of Sunday's election, with Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez saying he is confident of defying the polls.
"I cannot imagine us losing," he said, posing for
items.text:
Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
- Published
Spain's main party leaders have held their final rallies ahead of Sunday's election, with Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez saying he is confident of defying the polls.
"I cannot imagine us losing," he said, posing for selfies with supporters in red T-shirts and accusing conservative rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo of planning a coalition with the far right.
Feijóo's People's Party (PP) is narrowly ahead in the polls, and in the final hours of the campaign he travelled first to Barcelona and then Seville, promising voters a new political era of "truth, decency and good governance".
He accused Sánchez of evading questions on key issues like corruption, rail disasters, immigration and the national debt.
The Socialist leader heads one of Europe's few left-wing governments, and with the French presidential elections five months away, there is a real chance that two of the continent's biggest economies could move to the right in quick succession.
Almost 39 million people have a vote in Spain and while commentators expect a high turnout, most polls have suggested a close finish. Under Spanish electoral law, no polls have been published since Monday.
"This time, yes, we're going to do it," Feijóo told PP supporters, in a nod to his failure to form a government three years ago despite winning most seats.
If he gets to form a government this time, it will be with the support of anti-immigration party Vox, led by Santiago Abascal, whose final rally took place in front of thousands of people in a bull-ring in Valencia on Spain's east coast.
The venue was filled with Spanish flags and green Vox banners.
One of the biggest cheers of the night came when the secretary general of the party called for "less burka and less halal".
Ignacio Garriga said he was not acting out of hatred but love for the homeland.
We heard a small section of the crowd chant "Viva Franco" in reference to the dictator, whose death in 1975 heralded the start of Spain's transition to democracy.
A number of first-time voters at the rally said they were supporting Vox because of its policies on immigration.
Lledó, 18, said what had happened in Ceuta in the summer, when more than 70,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish territory from Morocco, showed that Sánchez was not able to control the country's border.
She had come to the bullring with her mum and aunt, Carli Chilet, who argued that Vox a"re the best for women's rights".
Vox is hoping to almost double its seats from the 33 it won three years ago. It backs policies such as "national priority" - putting Spanish citizens first for welfare - and "remigration" for foreigners not considered to be contributing to the economy.
- Leaders clash in final Spain election debate as housing dominates run-in 
  - Published14 hours ago
- Spanish election: What you need to know and what's at stake 
  - Published7 hours ago
- Who to watch in Spain's election race 
  - Published8 hours ago
- Clashing political visions reflect a divided Spain ahead of election 
  - Published2 days ago
The final day of campaigning was very much in the shadow of a four-way TV debate the night before that exposed Spain's sharply polarised politics.
All four leaders had solutions for the housing crisis. Feijóo said the PP would build a million homes over four years, while Sánchez said housing should be a right not an object of speculation and profit.
While the conservatives tried to turn the spotlight on the series of scandals that have overshadowed the Socialists' term in office, Sánchez and his left-wing ally Ada Colau, who heads Frente Amplio (The Broad Front), focused on women's rights.
The two leaders seized on a moment in the debate when the PP leader accused Colau and the rest of the left of staying quiet during a flood disaster in Valencia, briefly moving his finger to his lips. The word he used "calladita" is a diminutive and can also be used to tell a woman to "keep quiet" in a condescending manner.
Sánchez reacted immediately and called on him to show "a little respect", accusing him of sexism.
Feijóo sought to clarify what he meant on Friday, and accused Ada Colau of remaining silent during "these years of corruption". His decision to wind up his campaign in Seville was significant, because the wider southern region of Andalusia has 61 seats in Spain's 350-seat parliament, more than any other.
Andalusia is also important because it is run by a coalition made up of the PP and Abascal's Vox, as are three other regions, Extremadura, Aragón, and Castilla y León.
Feijóo has insisted he wants to govern with a majority, backed up by "parliamentary support agreements" with Vox and says he has never spoken to Abascal about giving Vox ministerial power.
Sánchez took to the stage in Madrid with his wife Begoña Gómez, and donned a red T-shirt that read "power of the people".
He then went on to praise Colau and her left-wing coalition's campaign. As he was speaking, Colau told a large audience in the south of Madrid that not only would they "not remain silent, we will win", vowing to form another "progressive government".

The legislation, app
items.text:
Venezuela to repeal law that bans opposition figures from office
It comes a month after opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned to Venezuela.
Venezuela will repeal a law that prohibits opposition figures from office, National Assembly Chief Jorge Rodriguez has announced.
The legislation, approved in 2024 and criticised for enabling political persecution, targeted those who promoted or supported sanctions against the country.
“That law responded to a very specific moment in a particular situation that Venezuela was going through,” Rodriguez said on Thursday.
The law was passed just after fraught elections which the then-incumbent Nicolas Maduro ultimately won amid widespread allegations of fraud.
An interim government headed by Delcy Rodriguez, the parliamentary chief’s sister, has run Venezuela since Maduro’s abduction by US forces in January. Delcy Rodriguez promised in September during a speech at the United Nations that the South American country will hold free and fair elections, without setting a date.
Since then, the US-backed government has been in political transition talks with parts of the opposition selected by Washington. That dialogue had reached an agreement to review several laws, including the one up for repeal now, according to Jorge Rodriguez.
Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado shook up Venezuelan politics with her surprise return from exile last month. Machado won an opposition primary in 2023 to take on Maduro in the following year’s election, but she was legally barred from running. The Nobel Peace Prize laureate is widely expected to run for office in the event of an election, despite her exclusion from transition talks.
Despite being shut out, on Thursday Machado launched a system of neighbourhood assemblies aiming to gather proposals for a future government programme and democratic transition. The assemblies are expected to bring together over a million people over several months, according to Machado’s team.
“We listened to neighbours who are breaking down barriers that many thought were impossible, debating the issues that will lay the foundations for the Venezuela to come,” Machado said on social media on Thursday after the meetings. “We are designing the transition to democracy, the Venezuelan way.”
Around 2,000 meetings with residents were organised in Venezuela and abroad on the first day of the initiative, her team told the AFP news agency.
Nineteen questions are asked during the assembly, with responses fed into a digital platform. Issues of national interest range from dates for the presidential election to changes in the justice, education, health, wage and pension systems, as well as the role of the public and private sectors.

“His main political platform is to say, I am not Sánchez, I am the opposite of Sánchez.” As Spain heads to the polls, what do Alberto Núñez Feijóo's campaign and political career tell us about the kind of prime minister he might become? Javier Carbonell, Policy Analyst at the European Politics and Institutions Programme and lecturer at Sciences Po in Paris, joins Gavin Lee to break down the Popular Party leader's efforts to avoid the mistakes of 2023 and keep right-wing voters mobilised without galvanising the left.
Carbonell explains the apparent paradox of Spain's strong macroeconomic performance and the difficulties many Spaniards face in their daily lives. “People still feel that their salaries are not enough to cover the cost of living.” Addressing the housing crisis, he acknowledges a problem he knows personally: “As young people, we are really, really struggling to find a house. He discusses the controversy surrounding Feijóo's “calladita” remark to Ada Colau, his lack of engagement in international affairs and the significance of his inability to speak English. However, it ruled that provincial lawmakers should be allowed to wear religious symbols in the legislature, Quebec's National
items.text:
Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill
November 27, 2026
Canada's Supreme Court on Friday upheld Quebec's ban on religious symbols for public servants.
However, it ruled that provincial lawmakers should be allowed to wear religious symbols in the legislature, Quebec's National Assembly.
Quebec's government passed the bill, known as Bill 21, in 2019, arguing it was necessary to protect its secular society.
Under the law, anyone receiving public services like teachers and police officers has the right to do so without being exposed to overt religious symbols, including hijabs, turbans and yarmulkes.
What did the Supreme Court say about the law?
Chief Justice Richard Wagner said that the law "is rooted in Quebec's legitimate and historical commitment to ensuring the (secularism) of the state in a free and democratic society."
Mathieu Levesque, the interim the right-wing Quebecois nationalist Future Quebec Coalition (CAQ) that passed the bill, hailed it as a "victory" for the French-speaking province.
"This is a victory for the Quebec nation and for [CAQ], whose actions have today been fully validated," he said.
CAQ ruled Quebec from in two parliamentary terms from 2018 to 2026, after which it failed to enter parliament and the pro-independence center-left Parti Quebecois (PQ), which also supported Bill 21, formed government.
The case was seen as a major test of how far provinces can go in defying provisions of the federal constitution by invoking the "notwithstanding clause," which effectively allows provincial governments to pass laws that may breach Canada's constitution.
Quebec invoked the clause when passing the secularism bill, known as Bill 21, expecting it to be challenged over constitutional provisions guaranteeing freedom of religion.
Critics argue secularism bill weakens rights protections
Critics have argued that the bill unfairly targets Muslim women and weakens legal protections for fundamental rights.
"This decision is an unrestricted license for every government in this country to pass legislation taking away the fundamental freedoms and the legal rights of every Canadian ," Stephen Brown, CEO of the National Council of Canadian Muslims, was cited by Reuters news agency as saying.
He said the law forced many Muslim women to stop working as teachers or even prevented them from volunteering in schools.
Emmett Macfarlane, head of political science at the University of Waterloo, was cited by Reuters as saying that the law amounted to "Islamophobia as a state policy."

items.text:
OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secrets as AI race heats up
Tensions between the two tech companies have escalated as intensifying race to develop AI products fuels competition.
OpenAI has sued Apple, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology.
The ChatGPT maker filed counterclaims in California federal court on Friday, saying that Apple’s employment practices were designed to “trap” employees and prevent them from working on competitors’ technology.
Apple and OpenAI did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters.
Tensions between the two tech companies have escalated as the intensifying race to develop AI products fuels competition for talent and proprietary technology.
In July, Apple sued OpenAI and two former employees, alleging misappropriation of its trade secrets to benefit the ChatGPT owner’s foray into consumer hardware. OpenAI has denied those allegations.
The litigation sets up a battle over who will control future AI devices that may not use traditional apps or operating systems — devices which, if successful, would direct consumer attention away from Apple’s best-selling iPhone. Analysts believe OpenAI is working on a phone or other device of its own.

items.text:
Putin unveils new Russian nuclear-powered submarine with hypersonic weapons
The Kremlin plans to expand its naval fleet with five new nuclear submarines by 2030.
Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has unveiled a new nuclear-powered submarine, which Moscow claims is the first equipped with Russian Zircon hypersonic missiles.
The Russians say they will add five more nuclear submarines to the country’s fleet by 2030.
Putin attended the flag-raising ceremony aboard the Perm at the Sevmash shipyard in the northwestern city of Severodvinsk on Friday, marking the submarine’s formal transfer to the navy, according to video released by the Kremlin.
“Russia is one of the few countries in the world capable of building powerful nuclear submarines of this kind, weapons with global reach and significance,” he said.
Nuclear-powered subs are a key part of Russia’s nuclear deterrent because their ability to operate covertly underwater ensures a retaliatory strike capability in the event of an attack.
Putin said the navy will receive five more submarines by 2030, including three Yasen-M class, the same as the Perm. They can operate in “any part of the world’s oceans” while carrying a range of cruise missiles, he added.
Putin also stated that Russia intends to continue modernising its navy and expressed confidence that all plans to build a powerful naval force will be implemented in full and on time.

items.text:
Capsized tanker carrying 7,000 tonnes of diesel to be towed away from Ibiza
- Published
A tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel which capsized off the holiday island of Ibiza on Thursday will be towed to the port of Cartagena, officials in Spain say.
All 17 of the Malta-registered Med Emre's crew members were rescued but the chief engineer later died in hospital. Six people were treated for minor injuries.
There had been concerns of a major oil spillage in the western Mediterranean but an inspection showed that the ship's fuel tanks are intact. An investigation is under way into what happened.
The vessel had been travelling from Algeciras near Gibraltar to Barcelona and is expected to arrive in Cartagena on Monday in what is being seen as a challenging rescue operation.
In a statement on Friday, the Spanish transport ministry said the tanker would be towed to Cartagena "as it is the only one [port] that meets the technical requirements to carry out cargo extraction and repair work".
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez told Cadena SER radio network he hoped the tanker could be taken to port "in the coming hours, in the coming days".
"The information suggests that, indeed... this leak is not happening", he added.
The Spanish authorities provided no details about how the diesel would be extracted.
Meanwhile, pictures have emerged showing emergency workers inspecting the tanker's hull.
Any possible environmental damage is being assessed by air and pollution control vessel Clara Campoamor, which is owned by Spain's national maritime rescue service.
Elena Delgado, maritime captain of the port of Valencia, earlier told news agency AFP that a small slick which had formed around the vessel had "disappeared".
"The situation is stabilised," she said, adding that further inspections would be carried out.
Regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz said the tanker had not completely sunk as originally reported. The vessel remains partially submerged.
The Med Emre capsized 25 nautical miles (46 km; 29 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia.
Rescuers in Valencia received a distress call late on Wednesday, according to Spanish media.
Minutes later, the vessel reported a leak and the crew said it was leaning at a 90-degree angle. It capsized in the early hours on Thursday.
Ibiza's marine environment was added to the Unesco World Heritage List in 1999. In particular, it is home to dense prairies of Posidonia oceanic seagrass, which is found only in the Mediterranean basin and plays a vital role in supporting local marine biodiversity.
In 2002, Spain experienced one of its worst environmental disasters when the Prestige oil tanker ran into trouble off Galicia's coastline, in the country's north-west.
More than 60,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil spilled into the sea.

items.text:
Charles Leclerc seeking outlier as Ferrari, McLaren, Red Bull try to catch Mercedes at Qatar Grand Prix
Mercedes dominated Friday's practice sessions at the Qatar Grand Prix and Charles Leclerc suggested Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull are missing something; watch final practice at 2.30pm ahead of Qualifying at 6pm on Saturday live on Sky Sports F1
Friday 27 November 2026 20:50, UK
Charles Leclerc believes an “outlier” has given Mercedes a “massive” advantage at the Qatar Grand Prix, after Kimi Antonelli and George Russell dominated Friday’s practice sessions.
Mercedes were nearly half a second quicker than the rest of the field at the Lusail International Circuit as Antonelli topped both sessions from Russell.
Their four-tenths advantage over closest challenger Lando Norris in second practice could have been even greater, with neither Antonelli nor Russell completing a full low-fuel lap on the soft tyres. It was an ominous sign for the rest of the field ahead of Saturday's qualifying, which gets under way at 6pm, with coverage live on Sky Sports F1 from 5.15pm.
- Qatar GP: UK schedule and how to watch on Sky Sports
- F1 2026 Calendar | F1 2026 Standings | F1 Gossip Column
- Got the Sky Sports app? Sign up for latest F1 alerts📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺
Mercedes' dominance was similar to their pace advantage earlier in the season but the second half of 2026 has largely been very close between F1's top four teams - Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren.
Ferrari were over one second behind Antonelli on a dismal Friday as Leclerc spun in second practice and Lewis Hamilton suffered an engine problem which brought his Ferrari to a halt.
"Honestly it's been a very difficult day. It's not that we didn't try on the softs, we couldn't improve our lap time on the mediums," said Leclerc.
"I lost the car and had some damage so we had to repair the car but that was the first lap of FP2 and I couldn't improve and even on the new soft later on I couldn't improve.
"A very, very difficult day. The feeling is just very difficult to get right. Not even on high fuel we were strong, so for now, it looks like a very difficult weekend but we are working hard to try and understand something.
"For some reason, Mercedes are so much faster than everybody expected, so the gaps are just a little bit strange, so there's something that's an outlier and we just need to find that."
Ferrari were not expected to be strong at the Lusail International Circuit due to the long flat out zones and high-speed corners but Leclerc suggested his team, along with McLaren and Red Bull were missing a trick that will give them more pace.
"I don't think we know yet what's the outlier. I think other teams probably didn't find that because Mercedes still have a massive advantage," he said.
"We are going to work towards that and analyse the data to understand what's going on."
Norris: Mercedes not even worth thinking about
McLaren were predicted to be very competitive in Qatar due to their strength in the high-speed corners but Norris and Piastri were never close to matching the pace of Mercedes.
On Saturday, McLaren are expected to put the new floor they ran in Las Vegas on the car but Norris does not think it will make a big enouch difference to catch Mercedes who are in "a different category".
"I don't know how much that will help around here compared to Vegas," said last year's world champion.
"But obviously tonight [Friday] we will see how much we can gain from that. It's not going to be the gap we need.
"We are probably seven tenths off the Mercedes a lap so it's not even worth thinking about them. But relative to the rest we seem to be in a good place. The fact we can have the new floor on tomorrow will add a little bit and a little bit is better than nothing. We seem in a relatively decent place."
Both Antonelli and Russell pointed out that Verstappen will always be a threat and the four-time world champion is coy about his chances of challenging the Mercedes in qualifying.
"A bit of a difficult day. The balance of the car is a bit too disconnected at the moment to go fast, so that's what we need to fix," said the Red Bull driver.
"The all-round balance is not there at the moment and is costing us quite a bit of lap time. We will keep trying and see how good we can get it."
"Mercedes look quite far ahead on the short run and long run. Let's see how much we can close the gap."
