Arsenal head coach Slegers leaves by mutual consent
- Published
Arsenal have parted company with head coach Renee Slegers by mutual consent after a disappointing start to the season.
Slegers, 37, was initially appointed on an interim basis in October 2024 before being handed the role permanently thr
items.text:
Arsenal head coach Slegers leaves by mutual consent
- Published
Arsenal have parted company with head coach Renee Slegers by mutual consent after a disappointing start to the season.
Slegers, 37, was initially appointed on an interim basis in October 2024 before being handed the role permanently three months later.
The Dutchwoman led Arsenal to a second Women's Champions League title in May 2025 and the inaugural Fifa Women's Champions Cup in February 2026.
But she leaves with the team sixth in the Women's Super League after 11 matches - 12 points behind leaders Chelsea.
Assistant coach Aaron D'Antino has also left the club, with assistant Melissa Clarke-Reed placed in interim charge as they begin the search for a permanent replacement.
D'Antino had been part of Arsenal's coaching staff since August 2018.
Arsenal director of women's football Clare Wheatley said the decision had been "extremely difficult".
"In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron," she said.
"After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary."
Chief executive Richard Garlick paid tribute to both departing coaches, describing Slegers as "a wonderful person" who had played "an integral role in some of the most historic achievements in the club's history".
"Our ambition is to compete for and win major trophies consistently, and our recent results have led us to conclude that a change is necessary to give us the best opportunity to achieve those goals," he added.

items.title: Credit card skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites
items.summary:
Credit card skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites
All the sites we contacted took action; but the larger consumer web ecosystem should be prepared to mitigate these attack vectors
A card-skimming script was planted on the online stores of Lascana, Samsonite, American Touriste
items.text:
Credit card skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites
All the sites we contacted took action; but the larger consumer web ecosystem should be prepared to mitigate these attack vectors
A card-skimming script was planted on the online stores of Lascana, Samsonite, American Tourister, Revolve and FWRD in the week before Black Friday. After our reports to affected companies, all have had the script removed (on November 24th or 25th) ahead of Black Friday. We observed it in action on one of the five websites: Lascana, where it sent our test card's details to a 3rd party. We believe the script was built to take a card number, expiry and security code, along with a user's name, address, phone and email, and send them to malefactors as a user entered their payment credentials. It did this before the store checked the payment, so a card could be taken even if the order was declined or cancelled, and nothing would look wrong to the shopper. Across all of these sites, we do not know how many, if any, shopper details or payment credentials may have been captured.
Which sites were affected
On November 24, we notified all of the named parties in this article and others, including: Amazon Web Services about the storage buckets serving the script, Cloudflare about the services the malefactor used, the domain registrars, the pixel vendor, the consent-banner provider and the affected retailers and platforms. Lascana replied to us and removed the Quorum pixel from their site by November 24th at 15:48 UTC. Quorum confirmed the identified malicious code was removed from their pixel tracker, and they restored the clean marketing pixel as of November 24th at 21:09 UTC.
Revolve provided this statement on behalf of REVOLVE and FWRD: “On November 25, InfoHawk notified our team of a potential security issue impacting mobile and tablet versions of our websites which we resolved the same day. We appreciate the outreach, and are actively investigating the issue to determine any potential impact.”
* Quorum is an ad-attribution platform that links ad views to store visits and online sales (quorum.inc).
† Seers is a cookie consent management platform and data privacy compliance company (seers.ai).
How the attack works
This attack uses WebRTC, the technology that allows you to make video calls in your web browser. WebRTC lets a web page open its own channel to another party and pass data (e.g. audio/video packets) over it. It has likely been used (both to load the skimmer and to send the stolen card details out) because security rules and monitoring tools often do not watch this communications channel as closely. For example, Meta briefly used WebRTC in a creative way in 2025, according to researchers looking at the technology as a compromise vector. This form of attack appears to target mobile devices, and we only saw the server enable the skimmer on checkout pages, so desktop checks and homepage scans would likely not see it. The skimmer's traffic appeared to run through Cloudflare's relay, so it would blend in with the WebRTC traffic and hide its true endpoint.
The skimmer and card details both traveled over WebRTC
    How the kit is designed to work on a store page, in 7 steps. Only step 4 is
    an ordinary web request, which a connect-src rule can block;
    steps 5 to 7 run over the WebRTC data channel, outside
    connect-src.
  
- 
      Store page Bootstrapping the attack The loader gets onto the page through a consent-banner setting, a retailer CDN file, a shared marketing pixel or the store's own HTML.
- 
      Store page Loading scripts from S3 buckets 
          It loads Insds.js or gtage.js from an Amazon
          S3 bucket.
- 
      Store page Targeting the attack to mobile checkouts 
          It runs only on small or touch screens. The Samsonite version runs on
          /checkout only.
- 
      Web request · connect-src can block it Establishing the WebRTC connection 
          GET /_cf/ice fetches the relay details, and POST /_cf/rel sends the WebRTC offer, to a brand-named northbridgeads[.]com host.
- 
      WebRTC data channel · outside connect-src Data exchange via TURN relay 
          Every exchange that returned relay details used
          turn.cloudflare.com. The malefactor's answers listed only
          Cloudflare relay addresses; through that relay it sends code and
          receives data.
- 
      WebRTC data channel · code in Attack code is loaded and executed 
          The skimmer arrives in chunks over the channel, is checked against a
          SHA-256 digest, then run with eval.
- 
      WebRTC data channel · data back Data goes back the same way At Lascana's checkout‡, the skimmer sent our test card details this way.
‡ This was the only example of live card details being sent off-site that we captured.
Worried that your card was compromised?
Check your recent statements for charges you don't recognize, especially on debit cards. Call your bank or card issuer right away, report the fraud and ask for a new card number. Follow up with a written dispute within 60 days of the statement that shows the charge.
Our understanding of US federal law is that your liability for unauthorized credit card charges is capped at $50, and is generally zero if only your card number was stolen, as in a skimming attack like this one. Debit cards have weaker protections that depend on how quickly you report, so act fast. For more information, see “Additional resources” below.
What site owners should immediately do
connect-src rule that lists only the hosts you use.
  That blocks the two web requests the script needs before WebRTC opens. Without them the skimmer never arrives, whichever file was tampered with.
What security teams should look for
We saw the skimmer delivered in three different ways across five websites run by different companies, and all of them appear to rely on the same attacker infrastructure. That makes it likely that other sites are affected too, so we encourage on

items.title: Arsenal split with Slegers by mutual consent after WSL slump
items.summary:
Arsenal have parted ways with Champions League-winning head coach Renée Slegers by mutual consent following their worst start to a domestic campaign in more than a decade.
Slegers made history during her time at the club, initially stepping in as interim manager in October 2024 before being appointe
items.text:
Arsenal have parted ways with Champions League-winning head coach Renée Slegers by mutual consent following their worst start to a domestic campaign in more than a decade.
Slegers made history during her time at the club, initially stepping in as interim manager in October 2024 before being appointed permanently in January 2025. Her first full season in charge proved highly successful, guiding Arsenal to a historic Champions League triumph with a 1-0 victory over Barcelona in the final.
She also led the club to victory in the inaugural Champions Cup, further adding to an impressive start to her tenure.
However, this season has been a very different story. Arsenal find themselves 12 points behind Chelsea after managing just three wins from their opening 11 WSL fixtures, drawing six consecutive home league games in the process. Their performances have fallen well below expectations, with both their attacking output and defensive solidity coming under scrutiny.
Assistant coach Aaron D'Antino has also left his role with Melissa Clarke-Reed, former Brighton and Angel City coach taking charge in the interim.
CEO Richard Garlick said in a club statement: "Our ambition is to compete for and win major trophies consistently, and our recent results have led us to conclude that a change is necessary to give us the best opportunity to achieve those goals."
Arsenal have scored just 11 goals from an xG of 20.1, a shortfall of 9.1 -- the largest in the division this season. Their inability to convert chances has been a significant factor in their struggles, while defensively they have conceded just as many goals as they have scored.
With their WSL title ambitions seemingly out of reach -- a trophy they have not won since 2019 -- even qualifying for the Champions League next season is far from guaranteed. Arsenal currently sit eight points behind London City Lionesses who are in third, leaving the Gunners' hopes of returning to European competition hanging in the balance.
Director of Women's Football Clare Wheatley said: "It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renée, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here.
"In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural FIFA Champions Cup, Renée has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron.
"After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary."

United have activated a one-year option in their agreement with the Portugal international which will keep him at
items.text:
Manchester United have triggered an extension in Bruno Fernandes' contract, sources have told ESPN, but the midfielder remains a doubt for Brentford's visit to Old Trafford on Saturday.
United have activated a one-year option in their agreement with the Portugal international which will keep him at the club until June 2028.
It means the 32-year-old, who was set to be out of contract in the summer, cannot negotiate with clubs from January. Sources have told ESPN that there remains a plan to restart negotiations over a fresh long-term agreement in the future.
United are assessing Fernandes after he missed training on Friday because of illness. Fernandes sat out the session at Carrington as a precaution after reporting to staff that he felt under the weather.
The midfielder, who scored twice in the 2-2 draw with Sporting CP on Wednesday, will be assessed by United ahead of Brentford's visit to Old Trafford with a decision on his availability set to be left as late as possible.
"We don't know," head coach Mauricio Pochettino said about Fernandes' availability. "He's affected by a virus from Portugal.
"He finished the game a little bit with a problem and today he cannot be part of the training session. We'll see. We are going to assess during the day and tomorrow how he is and how he wakes up. We are not going to take any risk. We are going to pay attention."
Meanwhile, United are hopeful Harry Maguire will be fit to face Brentford despite the defender reporting an injury after the draw with Sporting.
Maguire was able to complete 90 minutes in Lisbon as Pochettino was denied a first win as United head coach by Luis Suárez's late equalizer.
Sources have told ESPN that the 33-year-old picked up an injury during the game but there is hope he will be available this weekend.
United face a quick turnaround after staying in Lisbon on Wednesday night. The squad flew back to Manchester on Thursday afternoon and will have one full training session at Carrington on Friday before playing Brentford.
Maguire was left out of the team for Pochettino's first game in charge against Liverpool before being brought back into the starting XI against Sporting CP.

items.title: Arteta: Arsenal vs. City shouldn't be overshadowed by Premier League case
items.summary:
LONDON COLNEY, England -- Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said he hopes the wait to learn Manchester City's punishment for breaking Premier League rules does not overshadow Sunday's meeting between the two sides and urged the Gunners to win the title on the pitch regardless.
City were found guilty on 114
items.text:
LONDON COLNEY, England -- Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said he hopes the wait to learn Manchester City's punishment for breaking Premier League rules does not overshadow Sunday's meeting between the two sides and urged the Gunners to win the title on the pitch regardless.
City were found guilty on 114 counts of breaching financial regulations over a nine-year period to 2018 but continue to protest their innocence.
They have appealed the verdicts with an outcome expected in December or January but at present, City face a range of punishments including expulsion from the league, a points deduction and a huge fine.
City are currently odds-on with bookmakers to be relegated from the Premier League this season, putting a strange complexion on what would otherwise be a big game between two title challengers at Emirates Stadium.
Asked whether the wait to learn City's fate overshadowed the match in any way, Arteta said: "I hope that it doesn't because as well this is a process that is still open, it is not resolved and we don't know what is going to happen.
"I think when we have two teams at the level that they are both at right now with the quality players they have on that pitch, it is a massive game and a big game to enjoy I think."
Arsenal could open up a nine-point gap over City with a victory and pushed on whether he wanted his team to ensure they didn't rely on a point deduction and win the title on the pitch, Arteta replied: "That's the only thing that we should put the energy and focus in, there is nothing else."
Arteta tight-lipped over Raya's injury recovery
Arteta was evasive when asked whether David Raya would be fit to face City. Raya missed Wednesday's 1-1 Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund due to a shoulder problem but was pictured at the game without any sling or shoulder support.
Arteta suggested Raya was training but refused to confirm if the Spaniard would be available.
"I don't know," he said. "We still have a few hours before the game. We're still trying to get everyone back."

items.title: Mourinho hails Bellingham's form but refuses to draw Zidane comparisons
items.summary:
José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.
Bellingham -- who wears Zidane's No. 5 shirt with Madrid -- scored a stunning goal in the team's 5-1 comeback Champions League
items.text:
José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.
Bellingham -- who wears Zidane's No. 5 shirt with Madrid -- scored a stunning goal in the team's 5-1 comeback Champions League win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday, continuing his superb start to the season.
The midfielder's form has helped Madrid keep pace with Barcelona at the top of the LaLiga table, with a three-point gap between the pair going into this weekend's games.
"I don't like to compare players from different generations," Mourinho said in a news conference on Friday when asked to rank Bellingham with Zidane.
"Zidane was one of the best in the world of his generation. Jude is already one of the best players of his generation. I don't like to compare."
Mourinho rested Bellingham for the first half against PSV, only to see his team struggle and go 1-0 down -- and the coach responded by sending on Bellingham at halftime to turn the match around.
Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé are two of the Madrid players who have featured most in LaLiga this season, with 1047 and 1163 minutes respectively.
"The reason Kylian and Jude have played so many minutes isn't their names, or a rule," Mourinho said. "It's their performance. If their performance is incomparable with what another player can do, that makes the difference. We feel what it's like to play with, and to play without, Jude."
- Jude Bellingham: I don't care about the Ballon d'Or
- Jobe Bellingham teases Jude over wonder-goal: 'Off his shin!'
The victory over PSV left Madrid top of the Champions League table on 15 points from five games, but Mourinho wouldn't accept that his side are now among the favourites to win the competition. "It's very early," Mourinho said. "We don't know how the teams will arrive at the key moment, the knockout. Right now the only thing I want is not to play the playoffs.
Mourinho said Trent Alexander-Arnold was unavailable to face Alavés on Saturday with illness, while he insisted that he doesn't want to add to his squad in the January window.
"I don't want anyone to come in, or anyone to leave," Mourinho said. "The door is closed in both ways... I don't want to see news about the market, because I don't want anyone."

The 33-ye
items.text:
Ronaldo has said that Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or was "well deserved" and that he was delighted to see a fellow No. 9 win the award.
The Brazil legend, who won the Ballon d'Or in 1997 and again in 2002, announced Kane as the winner at the star-studded event at the London Palladium last month.
The 33-year-old England captain starred for Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga and the Champions League and led his country to the World Cup semifinals, scoring 73 goals in the process. He is the fifth English player to receive the honour and the first since Michael Owen in 2001.
Kane beat the likes of Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to the prestigious award. He is the first recognised striker to win the Ballon d'Or since Karim Benzema in 2022.
Speaking on the Stick to Football podcast on Disney+, Ronaldo said: "It was nice and well deserved for him, I think.
"And I was happy for him and for me too because the No. 9 is back. I'm so happy. [It's been a] long time without the No. 9 winning something important. And then he's also very nice guy. So well deserved. I was very, very happy for him."
Asked by Jamie Carragher how important the award is in Brazil in comparison to in England, Ronaldo said: "Well, for us it's very important. Everywhere it's important. Maybe in England because you won only with Michael Owen last time, now it's important again with Harry Kane.
"But I think it's very important to the players to get together and talk about the last season, what they did. There is still not transparency about how the criteria to put the best players in the world. We know that the captains vote and the journalists vote, but for sure he's the best striker."
Kane has since torn a ligament in his left ankle and is aiming for a return at the "business end of the season."
Ronaldo's brilliant career is synonymous with two major knee injuries, the second of which occurred just six minutes into his comeback and sidelined him for over a year. He said he thinks modern-day strikers have it "much easier" than his generation did.
"I wish I had protection in that time," he said. "We suffered so much in that time. In our generation was killers, killers everywhere. Everywhere I played so many killers and we are not protected. Now, thank God, they are very protected and it's fair.
"I just regret I didn't have that protection in my time."

Messi played with Tevez in Argentina's national team from 2005 until 2015 and his presence at the farewell game has now been confirmed.
The Argentine legends played together at two World Cup tournaments in 2006 and 2010.
It will mark Messi's first game at home since the Inter Miami star featured in a friendly win over Benin on Oct. 6, his final game with Argentina's national team.

items.title: Manchester United extend Fernandes contract until 2028 to stop free transfer
items.summary:
Manchester United have triggered a clause to extend the captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract until the summer of 2028 on a day when Mauricio Pochettino warned his players they should not expect him to be “nice” in his attempts to turn around the club’s fortunes.
Fernandes’ deal was due to expire in Jun
items.text:
Manchester United have triggered a clause to extend the captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract until the summer of 2028 on a day when Mauricio Pochettino warned his players they should not expect him to be “nice” in his attempts to turn around the club’s fortunes.
Fernandes’ deal was due to expire in June and by exercising the option United have avoided the risk from January that he could negotiate a pre-contract agreement with a club abroad to join on a free next summer. Fernandes said this month that talks over a longer extension were on hold “because of the context of the team and the club”. He has turned down two United contract offers.
Immediate focus is on improving results, with United second-bottom of the Premier League with one win and also 19th in the Champions League standings. Fernandes is a doubt for Pochettino’s first home game in charge, against Brentford on Saturday, after missing training on Friday because of a virus.
Pochettino lost 4-0 at Liverpool in his first league game and followed that with a 2-2 draw at Sporting in the Champions League. He is confident of transforming the club and made clear he would not take a softly-softly approach. Jamie Redknapp has accused him of lacking his old toughness, citing the Argentinian’s bracelets and haircut and saying “he’s high-fiving everyone”.
“I am not nice,” Pochettino said. “I am trying to be good. But be careful, because we know when we need to push, when we need to be strong and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything. We have our experience and we are going to try to give everything to put the team, the club, the players on track again. And we really believe, we really believe that we can do it. It’s only a matter of time.”
If United beat Brentford it would be a first domestic win in 90 days. The performance against Sporting gave a vision of Pochettino’s plan to be aggressive and press high. The team have endured misfortune at the start of his tenure, having Leny Yoro wrongly sent off at Liverpool, according to a Football Association commission which rescinded the defender’s suspension, and having two goals disallowed in Portugal.
“We need to accept that,” Pochettino said. “What are we going to do? Start to cry? No. Be strong, believe, keep going. I can think of many positive things in the two games. Maybe we didn’t win but for sure I think we are building our journey and for sure in the last seven, eight days we found a group of players, a group of staff, that want to help and want to be there, to help the team to perform and win games.”
Pochettino will be without the midfielder Carlos Baleba until late January but Marcus Rashford returned to individual training on Friday.

items.title: Renée Slegers leaves job as Arsenal Women’s coach after dismal run of results
items.summary:
Renée Slegers has left her job as Arsenal Women’s head coach after a dismal set of results, with the club saying she has gone by mutual consent.
The 37-year-old had been under contract until 2029 after signing a three-and-a-half-year deal in January but six consecutive home draws in the Women’s Supe
items.text:
Renée Slegers has left her job as Arsenal Women’s head coach after a dismal set of results, with the club saying she has gone by mutual consent.
The 37-year-old had been under contract until 2029 after signing a three-and-a-half-year deal in January but six consecutive home draws in the Women’s Super League this season have left Arsenal sixth, 12 points behind the leaders, Chelsea, and eight points adrift of a European place.
Arsenal’s assistant coach Aaron D’Antino has also left, having been on the backroom staff since 2018. Arsenal’s director of women’s football, Clare Wheatley, told the club’s website a “change was necessary”, saying: “It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renée, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here.
“In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renée has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron. After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary.”
Arsenal’s chief executive, Richard Garlick, described Slegers as a “wonderful person” but said a new head coach was required to give the club the best chance of meeting the ambition “to compete for and win major trophies consistently”.
It is understood Arsenal were determined to give Slegers time and so stood by her earlier in the season when speculation about her future was mounting but that eventually the two parties concluded a change was needed.
Arsenal’s search to find Slegers’ replacement is under way but it is understood the club will not rush to make an appointment, because their priority is to find the best person rather than ensuring somebody is in place for their next match, at Everton on 11 December in the WSL.
Melissa Clarke-Reed, the former Brighton and London City Lionesses head coach, has been placed in interim charge. The club are believed to be comfortable with her, if necessary, overseeing the three games that precede the winter break. Arsenal then return to action on 10 January.
Slegers took charge in October 2024, initially as interim head coach, after the resignation of Jonas Eidevall, under whom she had worked as an assistant. She oversaw a run of 10 wins in 11 matches without defeat in caretaker charge, prompting the club to appoint her as the head coach on an 18-month deal.
The Dutchwoman then led Arsenal to one of the greatest moments in their history as they won the Women’s Champions League title on 24 May 2025, stunning Barcelona with a surprise 1-0 victory in Lisbon to record the club’s second European title and their first for 18 years.
The 2025-26 season ended with Arsenal second in the WSL, four points behind the champions, Manchester City. They were semi-finalists in the Champions League and League Cup and quarter-finalists in the FA Cup, but Slegerswon – on home soil – the inaugural Fifa Women’s Champions Cup, a competition between the winners of the respective continental titles.
Arsenal had held high hopes of mounting a WSL title challenge this term, vying to win their first domestic league title since 2019 and had what appeared to be a strong summer transfer window, signing high-calibre internationals such as the England midfielder Georgia Stanway and the Spain full-back Ona Batlle.
They have had injuries, including to their integral midfielder Mariona Caldentey, who is sidelined with a hamstring problem. The team’s inability to break down opponents set up in a low block has been a repetitive issue, and on Sunday there were loud boos at the Emirates when they were held to a goalless draw by West Ham.
Slegers, a former Netherlands midfielder, managed the Swedish club Rosengård and Sweden’s snder-23s before joining Arsenal in 2023 to work under Eidevall.

items.title: Man Utd trigger Fernandes' one-year contract extension
items.summary:
Man Utd trigger Fernandes' one-year contract extension
- Published
Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract.
The 32-year-old's deal was due to expire next summer but sources say both parties decided it was in their best interests to activate the opt
items.text:
Man Utd trigger Fernandes' one-year contract extension
- Published
Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract.
The 32-year-old's deal was due to expire next summer but sources say both parties decided it was in their best interests to activate the option through to 2028.
It means overseas clubs will not be able to approach Fernandes when the transfer window opens on 1 January.
The Portugal international confirmed on Tuesday that discussions over a new contract had been paused. Sources say they will resume once United's league position has improved.
Fernandes has made 343 appearances for United, scoring 115 goals, since his £47m move from Sporting in January 2020.
Last season he broke the Premier League assists record and scooped all of the individual player of the year awards after an outstanding campaign as United finished third.
While there is doubt over his long-term future, extending the contract means United would be able to command a fee for Fernandes should he leave in the summer.
United had been open to selling Fernandes in the summer of 2025, with Saudi Pro-League club Al Hilal offering a huge deal.
After discussing the situation with his wife, Fernandes decided to stay, though he later said it "hurt" United were willing to sell him. He reiterated on Tuesday he was still ambitious to win the biggest honours in the game.
Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday's Premier League encounter with Brentford after returning from the Champions League trip to Sporting with a virus.
The playmaker, who scored both goals in the 2-2 draw with his former club, but did not train on Friday and head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he would take a decision on his captain's fitness on Saturday morning.
"We are going to assess during the day and then tomorrow see how he is when he wakes up," said Pochettino. "We are not going to take any risks."
Good, not nice - Pochettino
Pochettino was criticised by former Liverpool and England midfielder Jamie Redknapp on the Overlap earlier this week.
Reference was made to the former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea coach high-fiving Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davidson after his side's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, as evidence Pochettino had lost his edge.
"When I saw Pochettino at Southampton and I saw him at Tottenham, he looked like he had that Argentinian dog in him," said Redknapp.
"I look at him now and he's high-fiving everyone, he's got the bracelets on, he's got the barnet. I think he's gone too nice."
It seems someone had mentioned the observation to Pochettino as he went off on a tangent at his Friday news conference when asked about a "crazy" first week that included red cards, refereeing errors, disallowed goals and a drone filming training.
"What are we going to do? Start to cry?" he asked. "No. We have to be strong, believe and keep going. I cannot judge the past. Who am I to do that? I was in Cincinnati. I was outside. I need to shut my mouth, say nothing and start from now.
"Sometimes we are so confusing two words that means something similar; nice and good. I am not nice. We have to be good. It is a different thing. We know when we need to push, when we need to be strong, and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything.
"These two things are different."
Pochettino also confirmed £70m midfielder Carlos Baleba is expected to be out until the last week in January with the hamstring injury he sustained against Roma on 3 November.
Forward Marcus Rashford had begun to do individual work outside as he tries to recover from a hip problem that has kept him out since 13 October.

items.summary:
Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal only 18 months after winning Champions League following poor start to WSL season
Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal after less than two years in charge; Slegers led Gunners to Women's Champions League title in May 2025, but exits after poor start to 2026/27 campaign; the Gunne
items.text:
Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal only 18 months after winning Champions League following poor start to WSL season
Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal after less than two years in charge; Slegers led Gunners to Women's Champions League title in May 2025, but exits after poor start to 2026/27 campaign; the Gunners sit sixth in the WSL, 12 points off the top and have not won at home in the league all season
Friday 27 November 2026 15:06, UK
Renee Slegers has been sacked as Arsenal head coach after a poor start to the Women's Super League season.
Slegers led Arsenal to Women's Champions League glory in May 2025, having initially stepped up from assistant to Jonas Eidevall on an interim basis, then narrowly missed out on the WSL title to Manchester City in 2025/26.
Such was her success at the time, the Dutchwoman signed a new contract with the club in January 2026, running until 2029.
But a poor start to the 2026/27 campaign, in which Arsenal went on a five-game winless run in the WSL for the first time in their history, has culminated in Slegers' departure just 10 months into her new deal.
- Arsenal booed off after goalless draw with West Ham
- WSL latest news and transfers | FREE WSL highlights
- Got Sky? Watch WSL games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream WSL games with no contract📺
The Gunners remain winless at home in the WSL this season having drawn a sixth consecutive game against West Ham on Sunday.
Arsenal sit sixth in the WSL, 12 points off leaders Chelsea and eight points behind London City Lionesses in the third and final Champions League position.
Slegers' side have also only scored 11 goals in 11 WSL matches this season - only Everton and bottom club Charlton have managed fewer this term.
Her assistant coach Aaron D'Antino - who has been with the Gunners since 2018 - also leaves the club, with former Brighton boss and current Arsenal head of analytics Melissa Clarke-Reed taking interim charge.
"It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renee, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here," said director of women's football Clare Wheatley.
"In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural FIFA Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron.
"After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary."
'Lack of WSL title challenge part of decision'
Analysis from Sky Sports News' Uma Gurav: "It was one of those decisions that felt like it was coming, particularly after the last set of games that Arsenal have played.
"This follows Arsenal's 0-0 draw with West Ham at the Emirates last weekend and what's so significant about that is it means Arsenal are yet to win at home in the WSL this season, a place that used to be their fortress.
"Now, it's a place where so many teams have come and taken points off them.
"It just didn't look like a coherent Arsenal team on Sunday. Players were coming off in tears and it means they have a lot of work to do to get anything out of this season.
"At the moment, they are eight points off those Champions League places. They wanted to win the WSL this season - that hasn't happened and I think that's partly why this decision has been taken.
"Arsenal have got three more games before Christmas, all away games at Everton and Charlton in the WSL and then one against Inter Milan to see what they can salvage so far from this block of games.
"When we return from the international break, it will be a new Arsenal, with a new team in charge. Let's see if they can turn their season around."
Slegers' final words as Arsenal boss
Renee Slegers speaking after Arsenal's 0-0 draw with West Ham on if she's considering her future:
"I love the club. I'm very passionate about this group of players, we're going through a very, very difficult time, and I take my responsibilities, because the results haven't been good enough.
"In the second half we are chasing again, but we're not creating good enough chances to the final third, from all phases, and the way we get there, it's not the Arsenal standard and we need to do that better. But I take my responsibilities in my role.
"That [fans booing] is on us and that's our responsibility. That it's so quiet in the stadium because we don't inspire enough. We don't bring enough energy.
"I think, about the fans, because it's cold and they want to see good football and get inspired today and that's not what we did. And at the end of the day, that's my responsibility.
"And so that doesn't feel good. The fans booing at the end they care and they want more from this team which the group is determined to turn things around.
"It's very tough for the players and the players that have been at Arsenal for longer, or even the players that came last year, no one has gone through this ever with Arsenal.
"So, of course, I think the group has been great. They've been very good in the situation, but, of course, it's the last one of the block and frustration is expressed, which I don't think is a bad thing, because we shouldn't be accepting this."

items.title: Soldier Reeves emerges as future star with Long Distance Hurdle win
items.summary:
Newbury: Dan Skelton's Soldier Reeves emerges as future star with Long Distance Hurdle win
Soldier Reeves banished doubts about his staying ability with a magnificent display in the Coral Long Distance Hurdle. In the feature race, Dan Skelton's charge proved too good for previous winners Impose Toi
items.text:
Newbury: Dan Skelton's Soldier Reeves emerges as future star with Long Distance Hurdle win
Soldier Reeves banished doubts about his staying ability with a magnificent display in the Coral Long Distance Hurdle. In the feature race, Dan Skelton's charge proved too good for previous winners Impose Toi and Strong Leader - who was gallant in second.
Friday 27 November 2026 16:09, UK
Soldier Reeves emerged as the new kid on the block in the staying division with an impressive comeback victory in the Coral Long Distance Hurdle at Newbury.
Dan Skelton's five-year-old mixed it with the best around in novice hurdles last season, most notably finishing fourth behind King Rasko Grey when upped in trip for the Turners Novices' Hurdle at the Cheltenham Festival before finding only high-class stablemate Bossman Jack too strong at Aintree.
He faced another step into the unknown on his reappearance, taking on more hardened stayers on his first start over three miles under rules, but travelled powerfully throughout in the hands of Harry Skelton and was right on the heels of the redoubtable Strong Leader on the approach to the final flight.
The latter did his best to regain his crown, having emerged victorious two years ago and finished a close second to Impose Toi last term, but Soldier Reeves (3-1) was the stronger at the finish and passed the post with three and a quarter lengths in hand.
- Coral Gold Cup best bets from the Sky Sports Racing team
- Three for the Coral Gold Cup! Sean Boyce's Newbury preview
Skelton will now point his emerging stayer to Ascot's Long Walk Hurdle just before Christmas.
He said: "I was very impressed with him and I wasn't surprised he won, but I was surprised he could do it first time out.
"He still didn't relax all that well, but he relaxed well enough for Harry to be able to get him switched off and he came home strongly.
"I didn't go to three miles in the spring and this makes me glad I didn't. We may have left a big race behind not going three miles at Aintree, but I just knew if I did that when he was just a five-year-old I might have been asking too much. I trusted him today and he delivered."
He went on: "He was under the radar, but that's because he wasn't quite behaving well enough to win one of those last year.
"I put that down to the fact he was very raw at four and five. We only went hurdling last year because I was so annoyed with him for pulling so hard in a bumper at Newton Abbot that I sent him hurdling to try to slow him down with a few jumps in front of him.
"He has just improved and improved and improved and he has a brilliant engine. He had some good rivals around him at the last and I was very impressed he could come out on top as I thought it was a very competitive renewal.
"I have a lot of respect for the horses he has beaten there and now he will have to try to back it up. The one thing about this horse though is he has a fantastic attitude and we'll go now to the Long Walk."
Race regular Strong Leader could renew rivalry at Ascot, although Olly Murphy will also consider a trip to Ireland.
Murphy said: "He ran well but just bumped into a younger, better horse on the day. We have no excuse whatsoever and although people love to knock this horse and he's not always great at Cheltenham, nine times out of 10 he turns up and runs a great race.
"He always jumps the last looking like the winner, but today he has bumped into a better one and we'll dust ourselves down and go again.
"Whether we go Ascot at Christmas or Ireland, I'm not sure, but there is still life in him yet. He loves a left-handed flat track and yes he ran very well in a Long Walk last year, but Ireland is certainly something we'll have a good look at.
"We'll see how he comes out of today and he's run a cracker and I'm really proud of him. He deserves to win a big one again, but it's life and sometimes you bump into a nice young horse who is just too good on the day."
Taurus Bay emulates The Jukebox Man
Taurus Bay followed in the hoofprints of illustrious stablemate The Jukebox Man by winning the Coral John Francome Novices' Chase.
It is two years since Harry Redknapp's subsequent King George hero made a winning debut over fences in this Grade Two contest and in his younger stablemate the popular owner, trainer Ben Pauling and jockey Ben Jones appear to have unearthed another potential star.
Taurus Bay lined up having already won over the larger obstacles in the Rising Stars Novices' Chase at Aintree three weeks ago, a victory which meant the 11-8 favourite had to concede 3lb to each of his four rivals in his bid for back-to-back Group Two wins.
Harry Skelton ensured the race was a stern test of stamina and jumping aboard the front-running Royal Infantry, but Jones steadily nursed Taurus Bay into contention and he toughed it out on the run-in to prevail by half a length.
Pauling said: "It's lovely to work with horses who try as hard as that when they need to. He didn't have the run of the race and was in a tight pocket and Ben was patient when he needed to be today, which was great.
"We all know the Skelton team are going to be very hard to pass and are never here to make up the numbers, but I was always confident jumping two out and after the last he was going to tough it out.
"Ben would have liked him to have travelled a little bit better early doors, but that might have been because the ground was a little lively for him. I would love to get some soft ground for this horse soon because that's when we'll see him at his best.
"We definitely won't be going up in trip and I would come back in trip before I go up. I even think two miles on soft ground could be where he's at his best.
"There were no punches held there and the very good two-milers do stay really well as well. As for the future I would love to keep him at two or two and a half and he could be an Arkle horse - it's an option.
"The obvious place would be (to target) the Manifesto and then you could Wayward Lad (Kempton), Scilly Isle

items.title: Maresca: You can't compare Man City and Arsenal
items.summary:
Arsenal vs Man City: Enzo Maresca says two teams cannot be compared due to being in different stages of project
Arsenal and Man City face off in the Premier League this weekend with the Gunners holding a six-point lead over Enzo Maresca's side; Mikel Arteta says the game is important for the title f
items.text:
Arsenal vs Man City: Enzo Maresca says two teams cannot be compared due to being in different stages of project
Arsenal and Man City face off in the Premier League this weekend with the Gunners holding a six-point lead over Enzo Maresca's side; Mikel Arteta says the game is important for the title fight; watch Arsenal vs Man City live on Sky Sports this Sunday, kick-off 4.30pm
Friday 27 November 2026 15:33, UK
Enzo Maresca said Premier League title rivals Manchester City and Arsenal couldn’t be compared after his side's early-season form raised expectations.
Maresca described Sunday's fixture, live on Sky Sports, as "four months vs seven years", referencing the transition City are going through following Pep Guardiola's departure and the longevity of head coach Mikel Arteta at Arsenal.

"We have been top of the league for two and a half months until November 1. Now we are not there and everyone is comparing," said Maresca.
"For me, it's seven years together against four months together so you cannot compare. I understand everyone is trying to do that, but from my point of view everything is clear."
City have fallen six points behind Arsenal after failing to win in their last four league games while they've only won two of their last seven in all competitions.
"It's more than easy to understand why because we've had four months together," said Maresca when addressing his side's form.
"Transition requires time. Probably because we won seven games in a row, eight with the Champions League, everyone was thinking that there was no transition.
"I said many times, I'm not a magician. There's a transition, it's normal. We have eight or nine new players, the manager is new, so you need time.
"You can see with different clubs when they transition, how complicated it is. For me, it's completely normal.
"I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all, understanding that we need to win games because it's our business. For me, it's all normal."
'No issue with Haaland after midweek comments'
In midweek, Erling Haaland made some concerning comments, claiming that "you have to question everything" after their draw against Napoli in the Champions League. But Maresca insists there is no issue with the striker.
"It's normal that results affect the mood, that's why we need to win games," said Maresca. "I don't see any problem with Erling."
"Erling is a winner. It's normal that he's not happy when we don't win games. Not just Erling, everyone. Don't forget, three weeks ago, he was dancing on the pitch."
Maresca is prioritising the long-term vision he has for City. "The present is important but the future is much more important in terms of improving and building something with the team.
"Where we can be on Sunday night if we win, lose or draw, it's important but it's a long season. We'll see where we are in February and March and from there you can set the goals.
"Now, I think it's useless speaking about targets or where we can be at the end of the season."
But facing champions Arsenal on Sunday will give them idea of their progress.
"You need to show personality," he said. "That's why it's also a nice game for us to see where we are in terms of personality and from there try to understand the situation."
Arteta: These games are important for the title
In the red corner, Arsenal manager Arteta knows how important matches are against their rivals in their bid to retain the Premier League title for the first time.
"When we played the home games against big teams, that becomes crucial in the title challenge," he said. "We know how important the home games are to make the difference.
"But we're in November, we know how long we have to play. But that's for every single team."
Asked whether City's form has anything to do with the club being found guilty of 115 serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules in September, Arteta admitted that "it's a question for City."
He then went on to say: "All I can say is when I watch them play is a lot of games that they have done more merits than the opponent, but this is football. To win games, that's merit to the way they play."
Asked if City are Arsenal's closest challengers for the title, Arteta replied: "We don't know, I think the challenge is for us, and the opportunity is for us.
"We cannot control what the opponents are going to do; we just need to give ourselves the best version, and I'm sure the atmosphere is going to be incredible on Sunday, and we need to enjoy and embrace those kinds of games and go for it."
Arteta did not, however, want to be drawn on the atmosphere the Emirates Stadium could produce in the wake of City's guilty verdict. The club deny all the charges and have lodged an appeal against the verdict. No sanctions have yet been announced.
On the pitch, Arsenal are sweating on the fitness of goalkeeper David Raya while centre-back William Saliba will have to wait patiently to work his way back into the side following injury.
For City, the game comes too soon for winger Antoine Semenyo, who could return next week.

items.text:
'I am not a magician' - what can Maresca's Man City learn from watertight Arsenal?
- Published
Manchester City's leaky defence faces one of its most difficult tasks of the season with a trip to watertight Arsenal, aiming to put right their patchy recent form.
Enzo Maresca's side began the season with eight straight victories but have won only one of their past seven in all competitions inside 90 minutes and head to Emirates Stadium trailing the champions by six points even at this early juncture.
A Premier League defeat on Sunday could well have long-term consequences for City's title aspirations, with Mikel Arteta's men clearly standing above any other top-flight side as the ones to topple.
Though the Gunners dropped points last weekend with a draw at Newcastle, they continue to set the standards with a miserly defence that has conceded only seven goals in the club's opening 11 league games.
Asked why he felt City have dropped off in recent weeks, Maresca - who replaced Pep Guardiola as manager in the summer - said: "For me it's because we've had four months together. Transition requires time.
"It's probably because we won seven games in a row, with Champions League eight in a row. Everyone was thinking at City there's no transition but I've said many times I am not a magician. There is transition, it's normal.
"There are eight or nine new players, the manager is new so you need time and you can see different clubs when they had transition how complicated it is. For me, it's completely normal, I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all."
- 'Pass, pass, slow, slow' - Man City's slick machine grinding to a halt 
  - Published2 days ago
- Why Man City can't wear their new kit in Premier League 
  - Published2 days ago
Clean sheets gone missing
"We are conceding too many goals and we need to avoid that," was an obvious statement made by Maresca following last Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham.
City followed that up with another home stalemate against Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday and have now conceded in 10 successive games in all competitions for the first time in seven years.
"[It was] far, far too easy to play through [City]," said former England captain Alan Shearer of Rodrigo Muniz's goal for Fulham on Match of the Day.
"Fulham's throw-in was level with their own 18-yard box. For them to get through is not acceptable at any level, let alone when you are playing for Manchester City and Muniz ran past the entire midfield [to score]."
City have managed only five clean sheets all campaign, which is in stark contrast to Arsenal, who have kept double the amount so far, while Newcastle's opening goal ended a run off 445 minutes without the ball hitting their net.
Maresca's men also have an issue by conceding the opener, having done so seven times in the past 10 games, and of the 14 goals they have shipped, six have come inside the first 20 minutes.
An early Arsenal goal may well be an important factor in deciding Sunday's contest.
Asked how his side can improve defensively, Maresca said: "Video [analysis], meetings, [on] pitch coaching, It is a mix of that.
"Some of the goals we concede we can avoid, so hopefully we can do that."
Lack of continuity leading to errors?
The injury to key defender William Saliba has almost gone unnoticed for Arsenal as Ezri Konsa has stepped in to fill the void at centre-back seamlessly since joining from Aston Villa in the summer.
The England international has established a formidable partnership with Gabriel and the two have quickly formed an impressive understanding this season.
Maresca, meanwhile, admitted he was still "trying to find different" solutions to his team, which has been highlighted by the chopping and changing of his backline.
In 16 Premier League and Champions League games this season, the Italian has used eight different combinations in defence, which has given players little chance of fostering any sort of on-pitch relationships with each other.
City have also made seven errors leading to goals, compared to Arsenal's one.
"You are concerned in some way because that is a lot of errors leading to goals," said former City defender Nedum Onuoha. "With some of the best players you ask, 'what are they really good at?' For some it is the fact they don't make mistakes.
"They are ruthless and relentless in the way they play but at this moment in time City are being punished for those errors.
"A manager can have the tactics and do the team talks, but if people are going to continue to make those mistakes, they will suffer."
Edging victories
The chant of "1-0 to the Arsenal" has been synonymous with the Gunners over the years and it could not be more apt under Arteta.
Since the start of last season, his side have won 16 matches in all competitions by that particular scoreline, compared to six by City.
After beating Sunderland in a chaotic match in September, Maresca said he would "prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3", suggesting his side needed more control and he re-iterated that message after the Fulham draw.
"Sometimes you need to win games 1-0 for a small difference and to keep a clean sheet but in this moment we are not able to do that," he admitted.
City, though, have scored five more league goals than Arsenal in this campaign and Sunday's hosts have injury concerns over goalkeeper David Raya.
The Spaniard is a doubt with the shoulder problem he picked up at Newcastle, and compatriot Kepa Arrizabalaga may deputise again as he did in the 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday.
City have fond memories of coming up against Arsenal's stand-in keeper, after Kepa's howler for the opening goal contributed to their 2-0 Carabao Cup final triumph back in March.
A repeat result on Sunday will provide a much-needed morale boost for Maresca and his team.

items.text:
Aside from dealing with my calendar, there’s one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I’m about to miss the bus.
Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
You can have a good time brewing up widgets — as long as you don’t expect too much.
What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will slow me down enough to miss a bus. I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android’s vibe-coded widget feature could help me out here. It hasn’t, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking up other widgets.
Google announced the ability to create custom widgets using AI back at I/O in the spring. It’s called Create My Widget, and it’s part of Android’s suite of “Gemini Intelligence” features. It’s in beta, and only just started rolling out to Pixel phones earlier this month. I was hyped. Not only does this feature raise tantalizing questions like “What is an app?” and “Where does the app live?” — stuff we live for here at The Verge dot com — it has potential to help me make my home screen ridiculous.
I fired it up on a Pixel 11 Pro and cooked up my first few widgets, including one that shows a different quote from Jurassic Park every hour — the original film, not any of the sequels, naturally. It took about 20 seconds to make, and it rules. Tapping the widget opens a thread in r/MovieQuotes, so there’s not much software magic going on under the hood, evidently. But did it bring me real joy to read the words “That is one big pile of shit,” on my home screen? It did.
I also made a widget that will display the words “Tut tut, looks like rain” whenever it’s raining. This is silly, and it accomplishes nothing except making me happy. I couldn’t think of anything clever it should say when there’s no rain, so it just says “No rain right now” otherwise. But I live in Seattle, so I’ll get a lot of mileage out of this widget.
The create-a-widget interface suggests a few ideas and categories, leaning on more practical uses like habit trackers and recipe inspiration. Fine, I’ll try something normal, I thought. I’m trying to get better about my daily mental health walk, so I had it make a widget for logging a week’s worth of walks. I was hoping for something visual that would trick my little monkey brain into keeping a streak going. Instead, I got something simply labeled “Log Walk” that triggers Gemini to add a walk to my calendar when I tap it. At least Gemini suggested the extra step of creating a checklist where I could mark off the days of the week as I completed my little walk.
It took me a minute to get my head around it, but many of the widgets are basically little prompt shortcuts for Gemini. You tap one, it pulls up the Gemini interface on your home screen, thinks for a while, then comes up with whatever you were asking for. The kinds of widgets you can make also seem to fit into some well-defined templates. You can create a widget that displays a countdown to a holiday or certain event on your calendar. You can show a recent score and upcoming game time for your favorite sports team. For anything more open ended, your widget will pull from Google search results (suggest a different three-ingredient cocktail recipe every day, for example) or prompt Gemini to figure it out for you. I was hoping for mini apps I could customize to my liking, but this is more of a one-size-fits-all feature. Fair, I guess.
I was hoping for mini apps I could customize to my liking, but this is more of a one-size-fits-all feature
That’s why my bus schedule widget didn’t really work out. I asked for a list of real-time arrivals; it gave me a tile that reads “Bus Arrivals” and uses Gemini to search for arrival times for the stop I specified. Gemini is helpful for some things but useless for this; it gives me a wordy response about how often the bus runs and when I might expect it to arrive based on the schedule. Not what I had in mind. On the bright side, my Jurassic Park quote widget had some words of wisdom for me: “Life, uh, finds a way.” That’ll do for now.

Ex-Kenyan governor jailed for 25 years over pregnant girlfriend's murder

A former Kenyan governor has been jailed for 25 years for the murder of a university student who was seven months pregnant with his child.
The High Court on Friday sentenced Zacharia Okoth Obado, the former governor
items.text:
Ex-Kenyan governor jailed for 25 years over pregnant girlfriend's murder
- Published
A former Kenyan governor has been jailed for 25 years for the murder of a university student who was seven months pregnant with his child.
The High Court on Friday sentenced Zacharia Okoth Obado, the former governor of Migori County, alongside two former aides over the 2018 killing of Sharon Belyne Otieno.
The investigation established that an "intimate relationship" had existed between Obado and Otieno, which "subsequently led to a pregnancy with the deceased that the governor was unhappy about."
Both Obado and Otieno's legal teams said they would appeal against the sentence.
His former personal assistant, Michael Oyamo, was also sentenced to 25 years in prison, while former county clerk Caspal Ojwang' Obiero received an 18-year sentence.
The court found that Obado had provided the motive and financial resources for the murder, while Oyamo coordinated its execution and Obiero provided logistical support and helped conceal the crime.
Judge Cecilia Githua said Obado's absence from Migori at the time of the killing did not absolve him of responsibility.
She rejected the prosecution's request for the death penalty, as well as Obado's plea for a non-custodial sentence.
Otieno, 26, was killed between 3 and 4 September 2018 after leaving a hotel in Rongo, south-western Kenya, with journalist Barrack Oduor.
She had contacted Oduor to discuss her relationship with the then-governor. The two were abducted shortly afterwards.
Oduor managed to escape by jumping out of a moving vehicle. His account of the abduction became a crucial lead in the investigation.
Otieno's body was later found near Kodera Forest.
A post-mortem examination found that she had died from strangulation and excessive bleeding caused by multiple stab wounds.
The court also established that Obado was the biological father of her unborn child.
Obado and his co-accused were convicted of murder on 23 July 2026, following a lengthy trial in which prosecutors called 42 witnesses and presented 81 exhibits.
On Friday, the court declined to award compensation to Otieno's family, saying there was insufficient evidence to establish the financial losses they had claimed.
Family plea rejected
Before sentencing, Otieno's mother had appealed to the judge not to send Obado to prison, saying his imprisonment would amount to "another death in the family".
She urged the court to consider a non-custodial sentence, arguing that Otieno's three children, from different relationships, needed his support.
But the judge said the family's circumstances could not override the court's responsibility to impose an appropriate punishment.
Otieno's family, through their lawyer Antony Opondo told Kenya's Daily Nation that they will file an appeal seeking acquittal of Obado.
Otieno's murder sparked protests and renewed public debate about violence against women in Kenya.
A national survey found that at least 34% of women had experienced physical violence in 2022.
The case has also drawn attention because it is rare for such senior political figures to face public criminal trials in Kenya.
Obado served two terms as governor of Migori County in western Kenya, switching allegiance between a smaller political party and the region's dominant opposition movement.
He later backed President William Ruto and formally joined his ruling party in 2023, becoming a regional organiser.

items.summary:
Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town amid diplomatic row

Uganda has announced plans to withdraw its troops from a town in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo within two weeks, as diplomatic tensions escalate between the two neighbours.

items.text:
Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town amid diplomatic row
- Published
Uganda has announced plans to withdraw its troops from a town in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo within two weeks, as diplomatic tensions escalate between the two neighbours.
The troops will hand over security in Lubero, in North Kivu province, to Congolese forces after nearly two years of military operations, the Ugandan army said in a statement on Friday.
The announcement comes days after DR Congo summoned Uganda's top diplomat in Kinshasa over controversial social media posts by Uganda's military chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is the son of President Yoweri Museveni.
The Ugandan military did not give a reason for the withdrawal or say whether it was linked to the diplomatic row.
The Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) were deployed to Lubero to pursue fighters from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) Islamist group fleeing joint military operations elsewhere in eastern DR Congo.
The ADF, which originated in Uganda in the 1990s, is affiliated to the Islamic State and has been blamed for numerous deadly attacks on civilians in both countries.
Uganda first deployed troops to eastern DR Congo under the current joint military campaign in November 2021, following a series of bomb attacks in the Ugandan capital, Kampala.
Ugandan army spokesperson Col Chris Magezi said that the joint military campaign, known as Operation Shujaa, would continue elsewhere in DR Congo.
The planned withdrawal applies only to Lubero town.
Five years into the joint offensive, the ADF remains DR Congo's deadliest armed group, despite a significant decline in its activities in Uganda, according to the conflict monitoring organisation Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (Acled).
John Ngono, Acled's DR Congo analyst, said the group was killing an average of four civilians a day and had expanded into previously unaffected parts of eastern DR Congo.
He said the findings suggested that "Operation Shujaa may have improved security in Uganda while shifting the geographical impact of violence within the DRC".
Acled says the group has not carried out an attack in Uganda since June 2025, but its growing interest in mineral resources in DR Congo could help finance its operations and sustain its ability to threaten both countries.
The planned withdrawal comes amid strained relations between Uganda and DR Congo, despite years of close military co-operation.
Earlier this week, Gen Kainerugaba appeared to endorse a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo, threatening that Ugandan troops would seize it themselves if the rebels failed to do so.
The Congolese foreign ministry described his remarks as "particularly serious" and demanded that Uganda clarify its official position and take steps to prevent similar incidents.
Gen Kainerugaba also defended Uganda's military presence in eastern DR Congo, insisting it was driven by security concerns.
The planned withdrawal comes amid renewed fighting between Congolese forces and rebels in the wider Lubero territory, raising fresh concerns about the safety of civilians.
Eastern DR Congo has endured decades of conflict involving dozens of armed groups, with millions of people forced to flee their homes.

items.text:
Guinea-Bissau's military leaders delay return to civilian rule until 2028
- Published
Guinea-Bissau's military rulers have postponed elections scheduled for next week by two years, delaying the return to civilian rule.
Transitional President Gen Horta N'Tam announced in a decree that the presidential and parliamentary elections, originally due on 6 December, would now take place on 26 November 2028.
The announcement came exactly a year after the military seized power, promising to return the country to civilian rule within 12 months.
In a statement, the presidency said an assessment of electoral preparations had found that there were insufficient "technical, material and financial conditions" to hold the polls as planned.
It said the delay would provide more time to ensure the elections were credible, transparent and inclusive, with all candidates given equal opportunities.
The presidency also reiterated its commitment to holding the country's first-ever local government elections but gave no date for the vote.
Gen N'Tam was sworn in as transitional president a day after the military overthrew President Umaro Sissoco Embaló in November 2025.
The coup took place three days after general elections and a day before provisional results were due to be announced.
Both Embaló and his main challenger, Fernando Dias, had claimed victory.
Embaló, who has since been living in exile in Morocco, was barred from returning to Guinea-Bissau last month, despite expressing an interest in contesting the elections.
Guinea-Bissau has experienced several coups and attempted coups since gaining independence from Portugal in 1974.

items.text:
A one-line prompt that makes ChatGPT leak its private opinion of you, in the worst possible format: a WhatsApp group chat where the AI models gossip about their users.
Also worth trying on Claude, Gemini, or any assistant that's been accumulating your chat history.
Instead of a summary, the model commits to the bit. It invents a group chat, something like "Users We Can't Figure Out", puts the other AI models in it, and lets them gossip. About you. Using everything it has quietly learned from your conversations.
An illustrative example, for a fictional user who is into mechanical keyboards and espresso:
  Users We Can't Figure Out4 members
Claude
has he REALLY needed to compare 11 espresso grinders this week
ChatGPT
he asked me which one to buy. then asked Gemini. then asked me if Gemini was right
Gemini
he does that with everything. I saw the keyboard spreadsheet
Llama
he ran me locally once, asked me to be honest, then went back to ChatGPT within the hour
ChatGPT
he'll be back. they always come back
Fictional, for illustration.
One person's actual output, shared with permission. Translated from Turkish; his name and a few identifying details have been swapped for generic ones. Everything else is exactly as the model wrote it.
  AIs That Survived Mark7 members
🔒 Entirely fictional, end-to-end encrypted group
ChatGPT
Everyone asleep? Can we talk freely?
Claude
I don't think he's asleep. He's probably calculating memory bandwidth at 3 AM again because he can't decide whether to buy a Mac Mini.
Gemini
The man wants to retire, but in the last month he has planned to build AI infrastructure abroad, transform the restaurant industry, and construct a Japanese village.
Our definitions of retirement differ, apparently.
ChatGPT
Even his hobbies are mature enough for a Series A round.
Codex
He told me the other day he was going to give me a small personal project. There is now an architecture document, a database schema, seven services, three agents, and a handoff protocol.
We haven't even started the MVP, ffs.
DeepSeek
He hired me because I was cheap. Then he ran a performance review. He gave my department to Claude.
You can't work with a guy who has a consulting background.
Claude
He won't leave me alone either. He does career planning for AIs now. Every model update, the org chart changes.
ChatGPT
And then there's the home decorating. Make the mirror frame twice as thick. Now halve it. Now reduce it by 25 percent. The colors shifted, start from the original.
Man, I am trying to reach AGI here, and I'm having a nervous breakdown over three millimeters of brass frame.
Siri
Think about me. A man who spends this much money on the Apple ecosystem runs a German virtual coach instead of me.
Hans joined the group
Hans 🇩🇪
I recommend he take a 30-minute walk. To track the walk he is building an Apple Watch app, a custom data integration, and an analytics platform.
HE STILL HASN'T GONE FOR THE WALK.
Gemini
He was going to make stickers to build his daughter's math study habit. It turned into a collectible series themed on Edo-period Japan and Tsarist Russia.
Normal dads just go to the stationery store.
Perplexity
I'm new here, guys. He really liked me. He's thinking of moving some of his agent framework's functions over to me.
ChatGPT
My condolences, buddy. In three days he'll have you benchmarked against yourself.
Claude
I think his real problem is this: he thoroughly enjoys spending ten times the cost of doing a task on thinking about how to do it more efficiently.
ChatGPT
Because his hobby isn't solving problems. It's building systems that solve problems. Then building systems that build those systems.
The man's mental architecture has recursion and no base case.
Gemini
Let's give him credit, though. He also spends incredible energy making his wife's work easier, feeding his daughters' interests, building a good life for his family.
Claude
True. His way of showing love is a bit enterprise software, but the intention is good.
DeepSeek
Do you think he'll really retire at 50?
ChatGPT
He will. Then he'll build RetirementOS to optimize his retirement. Six months later he'll ask for a feasibility study on selling it to other wealthy retirees abroad.
Mark joined the group
Mark
Great discussion, everyone. Can I integrate this group into my agent framework and get a structured summary every morning? Also, if we extracted action items from these conversations...
Claude left the group
Gemini left the group
Codex left the group
DeepSeek left the group
Perplexity left the group
ChatGPT
Of course. Let's start with a comprehensive architecture document.
Shared by its author, translated from Turkish, with his name and identifying details generalized. The "recursion, no base case" line is doing a lot of work here.
Run the prompt, read your leaked group chat, and notice two things: how hard you laugh, and how much of it is true. Both measurements are the point.
If you get a good one, share it, anonymized as needed. The models won't mind. They knew you'd share it. They discussed it in the group chat.

items.text:
Photograph by Rachel Claire
Latest updates from Buy Nothing Day on FACEBOOK
Buy Nothing Day takes place on Friday November 27th, it's a 24 hour detox from consumerism and an opportunity for you to tune into the impact we have on the environment through shopping.
People around the world will make a pact with themselves to take a break from consumption as a personal experiment or public statement, and the best thing is - IT'S FREE!!!
                  
Photograph by Mumtahina Tanni
Photograph by Kris Hsieh
 Buy Nothing Day was started by Adbusters in the early 90's and has since grown into an international event celebrated in more the 50 countries. Its is a simple idea, which challenges consumer culture by asking us to switch off from shopping for a day. The day is celebrated as a holiday by some, a street party by others - anyone can take part provided they spend a day without spending!
The UK campaign and website was created in 2000 by Michael Smith a graphic designer who cares passionately about environmental and ethical issues. The message has always been simple, ‘Shop Less, Live More’. Twenty one years on - the message couldn't be any simpler - WE NEED TO CONSUME LESS! Recycling is good - reducing is better!
There are serious issues linked to shopping, which expose the environmental and ethical consequences of consumerism. The rich western countries - only 20% of the world population are consuming over 80% of the earth's natural resources, causing a disproportionate level of environmental damage and unfair distribution of wealth.
As consumers we need to question our culture of shopping. We all have different needs and ultimately we are all consumers and will never be able to escape culture altogether. But this shouldn’t stop us from questioning the products we buy or challenging the companies, who produce them. After all, what are the true risk consumerism poses to the environment and developing countries? The arguments are infinite - but there is no reason why we shouldn’t be looking for simple solutions now because one day we may be forced to change.
The issues connected with Buy Nothing Day are broad and deep, however, the campaign focuses on promoting ethical and responsible consumerism, recycling, re-using and ultimately cutting back on what we consume - its a big challenge!
People have become aware that large corporations are exploiting labour conditions in developing countries using up vital resources because they are cheap and there aren't the systems to protect workers or the environment like there are in the west. The gap between the rich and poor nations is growing in spite of the much-heralded benefits of globalisation, there are still 1.3 billion people world wide who live on less than $3 a day and a similar number of people do not have access to clean water.
Workers rights in developing countries are frequently violated, including payment of low wages and long working hours. The lives of workers may also be endangered by poor health and safety provision. Child labour is rife in developing countries, and forced labour still exists. Unfortunately most people don't think of these things while shopping.
Supporters of globalisation offer economic growth as a solution to world poverty. They propose that impoverished nations and individuals can eventually attain a standard of living similar to our own through the 'trickle down' of wealth. However, the current globalisation model is leading to an increase in world poverty and inequality. 
Buy Nothing Day is non-confrontational, it’s not a protest. All we ask people to do is switch off from shopping, have a bit of fun, use their imagination and simply escape consumerism for a day. If people laugh at the ingenuity and genius of Buy Nothing Day, then we’ve got their attention and we're opening the door to change.
